title.zh: 卷二十五 列傳第十五 王懿 到彥之 垣護之 張興世
title.en: Volume 25 Biographies 15: Wang Yi, Dao Yanzhi, Yuan Huzhi, Zhang Xingshi
title.raw: 卷二十五 列傳第十五 王懿 到彥之 垣護之 張興世 Volume 25 Biographies 15: Wang Yi, Dao Yanzhi, Yuan Huzhi, Zhang Xingshi

sentences.zh: 列傳第十五

translations.literal: Biographies 15
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 15

sentences.zh: 王懿到彥之垣護之張興世

translations.literal: Wang Yi, Dao Yanzhi, Yuan Huzhi, Zhang Xingshi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, Dao Yanzhi, Yuan Huzhi, and Zhang Xingshi

sentences.zh: 仲德少沈審有意略，事母甚謹，學通陰陽，精解聲律。

translations.literal: Zhongde from youth was deep and careful, with strategic intent; he served his mother with great reverence, mastered yin-yang lore, and had a keen grasp of pitch and rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Zhongde was thoughtful and deliberate, with a strategist's mind. He served his mother devotedly, studied the arts of yin and yang, and had a fine ear for music.

sentences.zh: 苻氏之敗，仲德年十七。

translations.literal: When the Fu clan fell, Zhongde was seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: When the Former Qin collapsed, Zhongde was seventeen.

sentences.zh: 及兄叡同起義兵，與慕容垂戰敗，仲德被重創走，與家屬相失。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Rui likewise raised troops in revolt and was defeated in battle with Murong Chui, Zhongde was gravely wounded and fled, losing contact with his family.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Rui had also taken up arms; defeated by Murong Chui, Zhongde was badly wounded and fled, separated from his kin.

sentences.zh: 路經大澤，困未能去，臥林中。

translations.literal: On the road he passed a great marsh; exhausted and unable to go on, he lay down in the woods.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed a great marsh, too spent to go farther, and lay down in the forest.

sentences.zh: 有一小兒青衣，年可七八歲，騎牛行，見仲德驚曰：「漢已食未？

translations.literal: A small boy in blue clothes, perhaps seven or eight years old, came riding an ox and, seeing Zhongde, cried in alarm, "Has the Han eaten yet?"
translations.idiomatic: A boy in blue, perhaps seven or eight, rode up on an ox. Seeing Zhongde, he cried out in surprise: "Have you eaten yet?"

sentences.zh: 「仲德言饑，小兒去，須臾復來，得飯與之。

translations.literal: Zhongde said he was hungry; the boy went away and shortly returned with food and gave it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde said he was starving. The boy left, then came back with food and gave it to him.

sentences.zh: 食畢欲行，而暴雨莫知津徑，有一白狼至前，仰天而號，號訖銜仲德衣，因度水，仲德隨後得濟，與叡相及。

translations.literal: When he had finished eating and wished to go on, a violent rainstorm fell and he knew no ford or path; then a white wolf came before him, lifted its head to the sky and howled, and when the howl ended took Zhongde's garment in its mouth and crossed the water; Zhongde followed after and got across, rejoining Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He had just finished when a storm broke and he could find neither ford nor path. A white wolf came up, lifted its head and howled, then took his robe in its teeth and crossed the water. Zhongde followed and reached the far bank, where he rejoined Rui.

sentences.zh: 度河至滑台，復為翟遼所留，使為將帥。

translations.literal: Crossing the river to Huatai, he was again detained by Zhai Liao and made a commanding general.
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the river to Huatai, where Zhai Liao detained him and put him in command of troops.

sentences.zh: 積年仲德欲南歸，乃棄遼奔泰山。

translations.literal: After years Zhongde wished to return south and abandoned Liao, fleeing to Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: After years in service Zhongde wanted to go south. He abandoned Liao and fled toward Mount Tai.

sentences.zh: 遼追騎急，夜行忽見前有猛炬導之，乘火行百許裏以免。

translations.literal: Liao's pursuit riders pressed hard; marching by night he suddenly saw ahead a fierce torch guiding him, and by riding toward the fire for a hundred-odd li he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Liao's pursuers pressed close. One night on the road he suddenly saw a blazing torch ahead guiding him; riding toward the fire for more than a hundred li, he got away.

sentences.zh: 晉太元末，徙居彭城。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taiyuan era of Jin he moved his household to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Jin's Taiyuan reign he settled at Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 兄弟名犯晉宣、元二帝諱，故皆以字行。

translations.literal: The brothers' given names violated the taboo names of Jin's Emperor Xuan and Emperor Yuan, so all went by their courtesy names.
translations.idiomatic: Their given names tabooed the posthumous names of Jin's Emperors Xuan and Yuan, so the brothers were known only by their courtesy names.

sentences.zh: 叡字元德。

translations.literal: Rui's courtesy name was Yuande.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was styled Yuande.

sentences.zh: 北土重同姓，並謂之骨肉，有遠來相投者，莫不竭力營贍。

translations.literal: In the north they valued shared surnames and all called one another kin; when distant kin came seeking refuge, none failed to exert himself to support them.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners prized shared surnames and treated one another as kin. When distant relatives came seeking refuge, none failed to support them to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 若有一人不至者，以為不義，不為鄉邑所容。

translations.literal: If even one person did not come, it was deemed unrighteous and he was not tolerated in the village.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who failed to answer such a call was judged faithless and shunned in his home district.

sentences.zh: 仲德聞王愉在江南貴盛，是太原人，乃遠來歸愉。

translations.literal: Zhongde heard that Wang Yu in Jiangnan was wealthy and eminent, a man of Taiyuan, and came from afar to join Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wang Yu of Taiyuan was rich and powerful in the south, Zhongde traveled far to seek him out.

sentences.zh: 愉接遇甚薄，因至姑孰投桓玄。

translations.literal: Yu received and treated him very coldly, so he went on to Gudu and attached himself to Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu treated him coldly, so he went on to Gudu and entered Huan Xuan's service.

sentences.zh: 值玄篡，見輔國將軍張暢，言及世事。

translations.literal: When Xuan usurped the throne, he met the General Who Supports the State Zhang Chang and spoke of affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan seized the throne, he met General Who Supports the State Zhang Chang and spoke of the times.

sentences.zh: 仲德曰：「自古革命誠非一族，然今之起者恐不足以濟大事。

translations.literal: Zhongde said, "Since antiquity revolution has indeed not been the work of a single clan, yet those rising now, I fear, are not enough to accomplish a great undertaking."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde said: "Revolution has never belonged to one house alone, but I doubt those rising now are equal to so great a task."

sentences.zh: 」元德果勁有計略，宋武帝甚知之，告以義舉，使於都下襲玄。

translations.literal: Yuande was indeed forceful and full of stratagem; Emperor Wu of Song knew him well, told him of the righteous rising, and sent him to strike Xuan in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yuande was bold and full of schemes; Emperor Wu of Song knew him well, confided the planned uprising, and sent him to strike Xuan in the capital.

sentences.zh: 仲德聞其謀，謂元德曰：「天下事不可不密，且兵亦不貴遲巧。

translations.literal: Zhongde heard of the plan and said to Yuande, "Affairs under Heaven cannot but be kept secret, and moreover in war one does not prize delay and cunning."
translations.idiomatic: Learning of the plot, Zhongde told Yuande: "Heaven's business must be kept secret, and in war delay and cleverness are no virtues."

sentences.zh: 玄情無遠慮，好冒夜出入，今取之正須一夫力耳。

translations.literal: Xuan's disposition lacks far-sightedness; he loves to go out at night rashly—taking him now needs only the strength of one man.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan has no long view and loves to slip out at night. Seizing him now would take no more than one man's strength.

sentences.zh: 」事泄，元德為玄誅，仲德竄走。

translations.literal: The affair leaked; Yuande was executed by Xuan, and Zhongde fled into hiding.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked. Xuan executed Yuande, and Zhongde went into hiding.

sentences.zh: 會義軍克建鄴，仲德抱元德子方回出候武帝，帝于馬上抱方回，與仲德相對號慟。

translations.literal: When the righteous army took Jiankye, Zhongde carried Yuande's son Fanghui out to meet the Emperor; the Emperor on horseback embraced Fanghui, and he and Zhongde faced each other and wailed.
translations.idiomatic: When the loyal army took Jiankye, Zhongde brought Yuande's son Fanghui out to meet the Emperor. Mounted, the Emperor took the boy in his arms; he and Zhongde faced each other and wept.

sentences.zh: 追贈元德給事中，封安復縣侯，以仲德為鎮軍中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Yuande was posthumously enfeoffed as Attendant Within the Yellow Gate and Marquis of Anfu; Zhongde was made Aide in the Army of the Pacifying General.
translations.idiomatic: Yuande was posthumously made Attendant Within the Yellow Gate and Marquis of Anfu. Zhongde was appointed aide in the army of the Pacifying General.

sentences.zh: 武帝伐廣固，仲德為前驅，戰輒破之，大小二十餘戰。

translations.literal: When the Emperor attacked Guanggu, Zhongde served as vanguard and broke the enemy in battle after battle, more than twenty engagements large and small.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Guanggu Zhongde led the van and broke the enemy again and again—more than twenty battles, large and small.

sentences.zh: 盧循寇逼，眾議並欲遷都，仲德正色曰：「今天子當陽南面，明公命世作輔，新建大功，威震六合。

translations.literal: When Lu Xun pressed close in invasion, the assembly all wished to move the capital; Zhongde with stern countenance said, "Today the Son of Heaven sits facing south in the sun, and my lord, born to the age, serves as chief minister; new great merit has been built and awe shakes the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, many urged moving the court. Zhongde said sternly: "The Son of Heaven sits facing south in full daylight; my lord, a man born for his time, has just won a great victory whose fame fills the realm.

sentences.zh: 祅寇豕突，恃我遠征，既聞凱入，將自奔散。

translations.literal: The demonic bandits rush like swine, trusting that we are far on campaign; once they hear of triumphant return they will scatter of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: These rebels rush like wild boars, thinking us still far away on campaign. Once they hear we have returned in triumph they will break and flee on their own.

sentences.zh: 今日投草莽則同匹夫，匹夫號令，何以威物？

translations.literal: If today we cast ourselves into the wilds we become common men; how can the orders of a common man awe things?
translations.idiomatic: If we now flee into the wilderness we are no better than commoners. What authority has a common man's command?

sentences.zh: 此謀若立，請從此辭。

translations.literal: If this plan is adopted, I ask to take my leave from here.
translations.idiomatic: If you adopt this plan, I must withdraw my service."

sentences.zh: 」帝悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 及武帝與循戰于左裏，仲德功冠諸將，封新淦縣侯。

translations.literal: When the Emperor fought Lu Xun at Zuoli, Zhongde's merit topped the generals, and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: At Zuoli Zhongde's merit surpassed every general's, and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingan.

sentences.zh: 義熙十二年北伐，進仲德征虜將軍，加冀州刺史，督前鋒諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yixi he marched north; Zhongde was promoted to General Who Captures Barbarians and given additional appointment as Inspector of Jizhou, directing the vanguard armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year twelve he marched north. Zhongde was made General Who Captures Barbarians, given Jizhou as well, and placed over the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡向洛陽，甯朔將軍劉遵考、建武將軍沈林子出石門，甯朔將軍朱超石、胡藩向半城，咸受統于仲德。

translations.literal: Champion General Tan Daoji and Flying Dragon General Wang Zhen'e advanced on Luoyang; Ning-shuo General Liu Zunkao and General Who Establishes Martiality Shen Linzi went out through Shimen; Ning-shuo General Zhu Chao-shi and Hu Fan advanced on Bancheng—all under Zhongde's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Champion General Tan Daoji and Flying Dragon General Wang Zhen'e moved on Luoyang; Ning-shuo General Liu Zunkao and General Who Establishes Martiality Shen Linzi went out by Shimen; Ning-shuo General Zhu Chao-shi and Hu Fan toward Bancheng—all under Zhongde.

sentences.zh: 仲德率龍驤將軍朱牧、甯遠將軍竺靈秀、嚴綱等開钜野入河，乃總眾軍進據潼關。

translations.literal: Zhongde led Flying Dragon General Zhu Mu, General Who Pacifies the Distance Zhu Lingxiu, Yan Gang, and others to open Juye and enter the river, then gathered the armies and advanced to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde led Zhu Mu, Zhu Lingxiu, Yan Gang, and others through Juye onto the river, then massed the armies and seized Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 長安平，以仲德為太尉諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When Chang'an was pacified, Zhongde was made Adviser to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an fell he was made adviser to the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 武帝欲遷都洛陽，眾議咸以為宜。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to move the capital to Luoyang; the assembly all thought it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wanted to move the capital to Luoyang, and most agreed it was right.

sentences.zh: 仲德曰：「非常之事人所駭，今暴師經載，士有歸心，故當以建鄴為王基。

translations.literal: Zhongde said, "Extraordinary affairs alarm men; now that troops have been abroad for years the soldiers' hearts turn homeward, so Jiankye should be made the royal foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde said: "Extraordinary moves frighten people. Our armies have been in the field for years and the men long for home. Jiankye should remain the royal foundation."

sentences.zh: 遷都宜候文軌大同。

translations.literal: Moving the capital should wait until culture and the imperial road are united.
translations.idiomatic: The move should wait until the realm is truly one under civilization and law.

sentences.zh: 」帝深納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took this deeply to heart.

sentences.zh: 使衛送姚泓先還彭城。

translations.literal: He sent Zhongde to escort Yao Hong back first to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhongde escort the captive Yao Hong back to Pengcheng first.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，累遷徐州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the Mandate, Zhongde was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Xuzhou with additional overall command.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor took the throne, Zhongde rose to Inspector of Xuzhou with overall command.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，到彥之北侵，仲德同行。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era, when Dao Yanzhi invaded the north, Zhongde went with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia, when Dao Yanzhi marched north, Zhongde went along.

sentences.zh: 魏棄河南，司、兗三州平定，三軍咸喜，而仲德有憂色，曰：「諸賢不諳北土情偽，必墮其計。

translations.literal: Wei abandoned the lands south of the Yellow River; Si and Yan provinces and three commanderies were pacified; the three armies all rejoiced, but Zhongde wore a troubled look and said, "You gentlemen do not know the north's true conditions—you will fall into their trap."
translations.idiomatic: Wei withdrew south of the Yellow River; Si, Yan, and three commanderies were taken, and the armies rejoiced. Zhongde looked troubled: "You do not know the north's true face—you will walk into their trap."

sentences.zh: 」諸軍進屯靈昌，魏軍於委粟津度河，虎牢、洛陽並不守。

translations.literal: The armies advanced and encamped at Lingchang; Wei forces crossed the river at Weisu Ford; Hulao and Luoyang were both left undefended.
translations.idiomatic: The armies encamped at Lingchang while Wei crossed at Weisu Ford. Hulao and Luoyang were both abandoned.

sentences.zh: 彥之聞二城並沒，欲焚舟步走。

translations.literal: Yanzhi heard that both cities had fallen and wished to burn the boats and flee on foot.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi learned both cities were lost, he wanted to burn the fleet and retreat on foot.

sentences.zh: 仲德曰：「洛陽既敗，虎牢無以自立，理數必然也。

translations.literal: Zhongde said, "With Luoyang lost, Hulao cannot stand alone—the pattern of fate makes this inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde said: "Luoyang gone, Hulao cannot hold—the logic of the situation is plain."

sentences.zh: 今賊去我猶自千里，滑台尚有強兵。

translations.literal: Now the enemy is still a thousand li from us, and Huatai still has strong troops.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy is still a thousand li away, and Huatai still holds strong forces.

sentences.zh: 若便舍舟，士卒必散。

translations.literal: If we abandon the boats at once the soldiers will scatter.
translations.idiomatic: If we leave the boats now the men will scatter.

sentences.zh: 且當入濟至馬耳穀口，更詳所宜。

translations.literal: We should enter the Ji and reach the mouth of Ma'er Valley, then consider further what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: We should enter the Ji River to Ma'er Valley and only then decide what to do.

sentences.zh: 」乃回軍沿濟南曆城步上，焚舟棄甲，還至彭城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he turned the army along the Ji to Licheng in Jinan and went up on foot, burning boats and casting off armor, returning to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He turned the army up the Ji to Licheng in Jinan, marched ashore, burned the boats, cast off armor, and withdrew to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 仲德坐免官。

translations.literal: Zhongde was removed from office for the fault.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde was dismissed for the failure.

sentences.zh: 尋與檀道濟救滑台，糧盡乃歸。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went with Tan Daoji to relieve Huatai; when provisions were exhausted they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he joined Tan Daoji to relieve Huatai; when food ran out they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 自是復失河南。

translations.literal: From this the lands south of the Yellow River were lost again.
translations.idiomatic: Henan was lost again.

sentences.zh: 九年，又為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was again made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he was again made Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲德三臨徐州，威德著于彭城。

translations.literal: Three times Zhongde governed Xuzhou; his authority and virtue were renowned at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he governed Xuzhou; at Pengcheng his authority and kindness were well known.

sentences.zh: 立佛寺，作白狼、童子像于塔中，以在河北所遇也。

translations.literal: He built a Buddhist temple and placed images of a white wolf and a boy in the pagoda, commemorating what he had met north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He built a temple and set images of the white wolf and the boy in its pagoda, in memory of his escape north of the river.

sentences.zh: 進號鎮北大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 十五年卒，諡曰桓侯。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died; his posthumous title was Marquis Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year fifteen and was posthumously titled Marquis Huan.

sentences.zh: 亦于廟立白狼、童子壇，每祭必祠之。

translations.literal: In the temple as well he set up altars to the white wolf and the boy; at every sacrifice he always worshipped them.
translations.idiomatic: He also raised altars to the wolf and the boy in the ancestral temple and made offering to them at every rite.

sentences.zh: 子正循嗣，為家僮所殺。

translations.literal: His son Zhengxun succeeded but was killed by a household slave.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengxun inherited the title but was murdered by a household slave.

sentences.zh: 仲德兄孫文和，景和中，為征北義陽王昶府佐。

translations.literal: Zhongde's elder brother's grandson Wenhe, in the Jinghe era, served as staff officer to Prince of Yiyang, the General Who Conquers the North Liu Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde's grand-nephew Wenhe, in Jinghe, served on the staff of Prince of Yiyang, General Who Conquers the North Liu Chang.

sentences.zh: 昶于彭城奔魏，部曲皆散，文和獨送至界上。

translations.literal: When Chang fled from Pengcheng to Wei, his followers all scattered; Wenhe alone escorted him to the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang fled Pengcheng for Wei his troops scattered; only Wenhe escorted him to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 昶謂曰：「諸人皆去，卿有老母，何獨不去？

translations.literal: Chang said to him, "All the others have gone; you have an old mother—why alone do you not go?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said: "Everyone else has left. You have an aged mother—why stay when the rest have gone?"

sentences.zh: 」文和乃去。

translations.literal: Wenhe then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhe then left.

sentences.zh: 升明中，為巴陵內史。

translations.literal: In the Shengming era he was made Administrator of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming he became administrator of Baling.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事起，文和斬其使，馳白齊武帝。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's rebellion arose, Wenhe beheaded his messenger and rode to inform Emperor Wu of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Wenhe killed his messenger and rode to warn Emperor Wu of Qi.

sentences.zh: 及齊永明年中，曆青、冀、兗、益四州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongming years of Qi he successively governed Qing, Ji, Yan, and Yi as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi's Yongming reign he served in turn as inspector of Qing, Ji, Yan, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 到彥之字道豫，彭城武原人，楚大夫屈到後也。

translations.literal: Dao Yanzhi, courtesy name Daoyu, was a man of Wuyuan in Pengcheng, a descendant of the Chu grandee Qu Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Dao Yanzhi, styled Daoyu, came from Wuyuan in Pengcheng and traced descent to the Chu minister Qu Dao.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝討孫恩，以鄉里樂從，每有戰功。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song attacked Sun En, Yanzhi, as a townsman glad to follow, won merit in every battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu attacked Sun En, Yanzhi of the same district followed willingly and won merit in every fight.

sentences.zh: 義旗將起，彥之家在廣陵，臨川武烈王道規克桓弘，彥之時近行，聞事捷馳歸，而道規已南度江，倉卒晚方獲濟。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was about to rise, Yanzhi's home was in Guangling; Prince of Linchuan, the Martial and Fierce Prince Liu Daogui, took Huan Hong; Yanzhi was then traveling nearby, heard of the victory and raced home, but Daogui had already crossed the Yangtze south; in haste and late he barely got across.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began Yanzhi's family was in Guangling. Prince of Linchuan Liu Daogui took Huan Hong; Yanzhi was nearby, heard the news, and raced home—but Daogui had already crossed the Yangtze, and Yanzhi barely made the crossing in time.

sentences.zh: 及至京口，武帝已向建鄴，孟昶居守，留之。

translations.literal: When he reached Jingkou the Emperor had already gone toward Jiankye; Meng Chang held the garrison and kept him there.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkou the Emperor had already marched on Jiankye. Meng Chang held the post and detained him.

sentences.zh: 及見武帝被責，不自陳，昶又不申理，故不加官。

translations.literal: When he saw the Emperor he was rebuked yet did not plead for himself, and Chang too did not speak on his behalf, so he received no promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned before the Emperor he was rebuked but did not defend himself, and Chang did not intercede, so he received no promotion.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年，補鎮軍行參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yixi he was appointed Acting Aide in the Pacifying Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year one he was made acting aide in the Pacifying Army.

sentences.zh: 六年，盧循逼都，彥之與檀道濟掩循輜重，與循党荀林戰敗，免官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when Lu Xun pressed the capital, Yanzhi with Tan Daoji raided Lu Xun's baggage train and was defeated in battle with Xun's partisan Xun Lin, and was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In year six, when Lu Xun threatened the capital, Yanzhi and Tan Daoji raided his baggage train but lost to Xun's ally Xun Lin and were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功封佷山縣子，為太尉中兵參軍。

translations.literal: Later for military merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Henshan and made Aide in the Army of the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for merit in war, he was made Viscount of Henshan and aide in the army of the Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍道憐鎮江陵，以彥之為驃騎諮議參軍，尋遷司馬、南郡太守。

translations.literal: When the Flying Cavalry General Liu Daolian garrisoned Jiangling, Yanzhi was made Adviser to the Flying Cavalry and soon promoted to Major and Administrator of Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Flying Cavalry General Liu Daolian garrisoned Jiangling, Yanzhi became his adviser, then major and administrator of Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 又從文帝西鎮，除使持節、南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: He again followed the Prince of Pengcheng west to garrison and was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Colonel Director of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Pengcheng west to garrison and was made bearer of the staff and colonel directing the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When the Emperor received the Mandate, Yanzhi was advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor took the throne Yanzhi was raised to marquis.

sentences.zh: 彥之佐守荊楚，垂二十載，威信為士庶所懷。

translations.literal: Yanzhi assisted in holding Jing and Chu for nearly twenty years; his authority and trust were cherished by gentry and commoners alike.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years he helped hold Jing and Chu; gentry and commoners alike trusted him.

sentences.zh: 及文帝入奉大統，以徐羨之等新有篡虐，懼，欲使彥之領兵前驅。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Pengcheng entered to uphold the great succession, because Xu Xianzhi and the others had newly committed usurpation and cruelty, he feared and wished to have Yanzhi lead troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered to uphold the succession, fearing Xu Xianzhi's recent usurpation and cruelty, he wanted Yanzhi to lead troops ahead.

sentences.zh: 彥之曰：「了彼不貳，便應朝服順流；

translations.literal: Yanzhi said, "If they are finished with disloyalty, one should go in court dress down the current;"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi said: "If they are truly loyal, go in court dress downriver;"

sentences.zh: 若使有虞，此師既不足恃，更開嫌隙之端，非所以副遠邇之望也。

translations.literal: if there is cause for suspicion, this force is not enough to rely on, and opening a further rift is not how to answer the hopes of near and far.
translations.idiomatic: if there is doubt, this army is too small to trust, and opening fresh suspicion will not satisfy men near or far."

sentences.zh: 」會雍州刺史褚叔度卒，乃遣彥之權鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: When the Inspector of Yongzhou Chu Shudu died, Yanzhi was sent to garrison Xiangyang in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector of Yongzhou Chu Shudu died, Yanzhi was sent to hold Xiangyang in his place.

sentences.zh: 羨之等欲即以彥之為雍州，上不許，徵為中領軍，委以戎政。

translations.literal: Xianzhi and the others wished at once to make Yanzhi Inspector of Yongzhou; the Emperor did not permit it and summoned him as Director of the Central Guard, entrusting him with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi wanted him made inspector of Yongzhou; the Emperor refused and recalled him as director of the central guard, entrusting him with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 彥之自襄陽下，謝晦已至鎮，慮彥之不過己，彥之至楊口，步往江陵，深布誠款，晦亦厚自結納。

translations.literal: Yanzhi came down from Xiangyang; Xie Hui had already reached his post and feared Yanzhi would not defer to him; Yanzhi reached Yangkou, went on foot to Jiangling, and laid out his sincerity in full; Hui too bound himself to him warmly.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi came down from Xiangyang. Xie Hui, already in post, feared he would not defer; Yanzhi went on foot from Yangkou to Jiangling, opened his heart fully, and Hui responded with warm trust.

sentences.zh: 彥之留馬及利劍名刀以與晦，晦由此大安。

translations.literal: Yanzhi left horses and sharp swords and famous blades for Hui; by this Hui was greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: He left horses, fine swords, and famous blades with Hui, and Hui was greatly reassured.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年討晦，進彥之鎮軍，于彭城洲戰不利，咸欲退還夏口，彥之不回。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia, in the campaign against Hui, Yanzhi was promoted to Pacifying General; at Pengcheng Isle the battle went badly and all wished to withdraw to Xiakou, but Yanzhi would not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year three, campaigning against Hui, Yanzhi was made Pacifying General. At Pengcheng Isle the battle went badly and all wanted to fall back to Xiakou; Yanzhi would not retreat.

sentences.zh: 會檀道濟至，晦乃敗走。

translations.literal: When Tan Daoji arrived, Hui was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan Daoji arrived Hui was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，因監荊州州府事，改封建昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, Yanzhi supervised Jingzhou's prefectural affairs and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling fell he oversaw Jingzhou's prefectural affairs and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 其秋，遷南豫州刺史、監六州諸軍事，鎮曆陽。

translations.literal: That autumn he was moved to Inspector of South Yuzhou, overseeing six provinces' military affairs, garrisoning Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he became inspector of South Yuzhou, overseeing six provinces, with his seat at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 上於彥之恩厚，將加開府，欲先令立功。

translations.literal: The Emperor's favor toward Yanzhi was thick; he wished to grant an opening of a separate office and wanted him first to achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor favored Yanzhi deeply and planned to grant him a separate office once he had won fresh merit.

sentences.zh: 七年，遣彥之制督王仲德、竺靈秀、尹沖、段宏、趙伯符、竺靈真、庾俊之、朱修之等北侵，自淮入泗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he sent Yanzhi to command Wang Zhongde, Zhu Lingxiu, Yin Chong, Duan Hong, Zhao Bofu, Zhu Lingzhen, Yu Junzhi, Zhu Xiuzhi, and others north, entering the Si from the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he sent Yanzhi to command Wang Zhongde, Zhu Lingxiu, Yin Chong, Duan Hong, Zhao Bofu, Zhu Lingzhen, Yu Junzhi, Zhu Xiuzhi, and others north from the Huai into the Si.

sentences.zh: 泗水滲，日裁行十里。

translations.literal: The Si water seeped away; each day they could advance only ten li.
translations.idiomatic: The Si ran low; they advanced barely ten li a day.

sentences.zh: 自四月至七月，始至東平須昌縣。

translations.literal: From the fourth month to the seventh they at last reached Xuchang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth month to the seventh they at last reached Xuchang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 魏滑台、虎牢、洛陽守兵並走。

translations.literal: Wei's garrisons at Huatai, Hulao, and Luoyang all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's garrisons at Huatai, Hulao, and Luoyang all abandoned their posts.

sentences.zh: 彥之留朱修之守滑台，尹沖守虎牢，杜驥守金墉。

translations.literal: Yanzhi left Zhu Xiuzhi to hold Huatai, Yin Chong to hold Hulao, and Du Ji to hold Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi left Zhu Xiuzhi at Huatai, Yin Chong at Hulao, and Du Ji at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 十月，魏軍向金墉城，次至虎牢，杜驥奔走，尹沖眾潰而死。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Wei forces moved on Jinyong, then reached Hulao; Du Ji fled, Yin Chong's troops collapsed and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Wei moved on Jinyong, then Hulao. Du Ji fled; Yin Chong's force broke and he died.

sentences.zh: 魏軍仍進滑台。

translations.literal: Wei forces then advanced on Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then pressed Huatai.

sentences.zh: 時河冰將合，糧食又罄，彥之先有目疾，至是大動，將士疾疫，乃回軍，焚舟步至彭城。

translations.literal: At that time the river ice was about to close and provisions were exhausted; Yanzhi had had an eye ailment before, and now it flared badly; officers and soldiers fell to plague; he turned the army back, burned the boats, and went on foot to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The river was about to freeze and food was gone. Yanzhi's old eye trouble worsened; plague swept the ranks. He turned back, burned the boats, and marched to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 初遣彥之，資實甚盛，及還，凡百蕩盡，府藏為空。

translations.literal: When Yanzhi was first sent out, supplies and wealth were very abundant; on return everything was swept away and the treasury empty.
translations.idiomatic: He had set out richly supplied; he returned stripped bare, the treasury empty.

sentences.zh: 文帝遣檀道濟北救滑台，收彥之下獄，免官。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent Tan Daoji north to relieve Huatai, put Yanzhi in prison, and removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Tan Daoji to relieve Huatai, imprisoned Yanzhi, and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史竺靈秀棄軍伏誅。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Zhu Lingxiu abandoned the army and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Yanzhou Zhu Lingxiu deserted and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，起為護軍。

translations.literal: The next summer he was recalled as Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: The following summer he was recalled as Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 九年，復封邑，固辭。

translations.literal: In the ninth year his fief was restored; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine his fief was restored; he refused firmly.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，乃復先戶邑，諡曰忠公。

translations.literal: The next year he died; then his former household fief was restored; his posthumous title was Duke Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: He died the next year; his former fief was then restored, and he was posthumously titled Duke Zhong.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，詔彥之與王華、王曇首配食文帝廟庭。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian an edict paired Yanzhi with Wang Hua and Wang Tanshou for sacrifice in Emperor Wen's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaojian year three an edict joined Yanzhi with Wang Hua and Wang Tanshou in sacrifice at Emperor Wen's temple.

sentences.zh: 長子元度位益州刺史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yuandu held the post of Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yuandu served as inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 少子仲度嗣，位驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: His younger son Zhongdu succeeded and held the post of Attendant in the Flying Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His younger son Zhongdu inherited and served as attendant in the Flying Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並有才用，皆早卒。

translations.literal: The brothers all had talent and use but died young.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers were all capable but died young.

sentences.zh: 仲度子撝。

translations.literal: Zhongdu's son Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdu's son was Hui.

sentences.zh: 撝字茂謙。

translations.literal: Hui's courtesy name was Maoqian.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was styled Maoqian.

sentences.zh: 襲爵建昌公。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the dukedom of Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝立，欲收物情，以撝功臣之後，自長兼左戶郎中擢為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming of Song was established and wished to win men's hearts, because Hui was the descendant of a meritorious minister, from senior concurrent Left Household Lang he was raised to Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne and sought popular favor, he raised Hui—heir of a founding minister—from senior concurrent Left Household Lang to palace aide to the heir.

sentences.zh: 撝資藉豪富，厚自奉養，供一身一月十萬。

translations.literal: Hui's family background was grand and rich; he supported himself lavishly—a hundred thousand for himself alone each month.
translations.idiomatic: Hui came from great wealth and spent lavishly on himself alone— a hundred thousand a month.

sentences.zh: 宅宇山池，伎妾姿藝，皆窮上品。

translations.literal: His residence, hills, and pools, his singing-girls' beauty and skill—all were of the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: House, gardens, pools, and the beauty and skill of his entertainers were all of the finest.

sentences.zh: 才調流贍，善納交遊。

translations.literal: His talent and style flowed richly; he was skilled at making friends.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and fluent, he excelled at friendship.

sentences.zh: 愛伎陳玉珠，明帝遣求不與，逼奪之，撝頗怨，帝令有司誣奏，將殺之。

translations.literal: He loved the singing-girl Chen Yuzhu; Emperor Ming sent to ask for her and Hui would not give her; the Emperor forced her away; Hui was much resentful, and the Emperor had the authorities frame a charge and planned to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the singer Chen Yuzhu. Emperor Ming demanded her; Hui refused; the Emperor seized her. Resentful, Hui drew a framed charge and a death sentence.

sentences.zh: 撝入獄，數宿須鬢皆白，免死，系尚方。

translations.literal: Hui entered prison; in a few nights his beard and temples all turned white; he was spared death and held in the Imperial Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: In prison his beard and temples whitened in days. Spared death, he was held in the Imperial Workshop.

sentences.zh: 奪封與弟賁，撝由是更以貶素自立。

translations.literal: His fief was taken and given to his younger brother Ben; Hui thereafter changed to plain living and stood on his own.
translations.idiomatic: His fief went to his brother Ben; thereafter Hui lived plainly and stood on his own.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，弟賁讓封還撝，朝議許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, his younger brother Ben returned the fief to Hui; court opinion approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Ben returned the fief; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 沆字茂瀣，幼聰敏，五歲時，父撝于屏風抄古詩，沆請教讀一遍，便能諷誦。

translations.literal: Hang, courtesy name Maoxie, was clever from childhood; at five, when his father Hui copied ancient poems on a screen, Hang asked to be taught and after one reading could recite them.
translations.idiomatic: Hang, styled Maoxie, was clever as a child. At five, when Hui copied old poems on a screen, Hang asked to learn them and could recite after one reading.

sentences.zh: 及長，善屬文，工篆隸，美風神，容止可悅。

translations.literal: When grown he was skilled at composing prose, adept at seal and clerical script, with fine spirit and bearing pleasant to behold.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he wrote well, mastered seal and clerical script, and had a pleasing presence.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，為征虜主簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang's Tianjian era he was Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Liang's Tianjian reign he was chief clerk to the General Who Conquers Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，以為太子洗馬。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established he was made Palace Aide to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was set up he became palace aide to the heir.

sentences.zh: 時文德殿置學士省，召高才碩學待詔，沆通籍焉。

translations.literal: At that time the Wende Hall set up a Scholars' Office and summoned men of high talent and great learning to await edicts; Hang held registry there.
translations.idiomatic: The Wende Hall opened a Scholars' Office for eminent scholars awaiting edicts; Hang held registry there.

sentences.zh: 武帝宴華光殿，命群臣賦詩，獨詔沆為二百字，三刻便成。

translations.literal: The Emperor feasted at Huaguang Hall and ordered the ministers to compose poems, singling out Hang alone for two hundred characters to be done in three quarters of an hour.
translations.idiomatic: At a feast in Huaguang Hall the Emperor ordered poems; Hang alone was told to write two hundred characters in three quarters of an hour.

sentences.zh: 沆於坐立奏，其文甚美。

translations.literal: Hang composed standing and sitting and presented it; the text was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Hang composed on the spot and presented it; the piece was excellent.

sentences.zh: 俄以洗馬管東宮書記及散騎省優策文。

translations.literal: Soon as palace aide he managed Eastern Palace records and superior policy essays in the Palace Attendant office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he managed Eastern Palace records and superior policy essays as palace aide.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔尚書郎在職清能者為侍郎，以沆為殿中曹侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict said that active Masters of Writing of clear ability should serve as Attendants; Hang was made Attendant of the Hall Central Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In year three an edict made active, able Masters of Writing into attendants; Hang became attendant of the Hall Central Bureau.

sentences.zh: 此曹以文才選，沆從父兄溉、洽並有才名，時相代為之，見榮當世。

translations.literal: This bureau was chosen for literary talent; Hang's father's elder brother's sons Gai and Qia both had fame for talent; at the time they alternated in the post and were honored in the age.
translations.idiomatic: That bureau chose literary talent. Hang's cousins Gai and Qia were both famed; they alternated in the post and were honored in their day.

sentences.zh: 遷太子中舍人。

translations.literal: He was moved to Palace Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace cadet.

sentences.zh: 沆為人謙敬，口不論人短。

translations.literal: Hang was modest and respectful in person and did not discuss others' faults in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Hang was modest and never spoke ill of others.

sentences.zh: 任昉、範雲皆與善。

translations.literal: Ren Fang and Fan Yun were both on good terms with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang and Fan Yun were both his friends.

sentences.zh: 後卒于北中郎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Later he died as Adviser to the General of the North.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as adviser to the General of the North.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦百餘篇。

translations.literal: His collected poems and rhapsodies numbered more than a hundred pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He left more than a hundred poems and rhapsodies.

sentences.zh: 溉字茂灌，撝弟子也。

translations.literal: Gai, courtesy name Maoguan, was Hui's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Gai, styled Maoguan, was Hui's nephew.

sentences.zh: 父坦，齊中書郎。

translations.literal: His father Tan was Master of Writing in Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan had been Master of Writing under Qi.

sentences.zh: 溉少孤貧，與兄沼弟洽俱知名，起家王國左常侍。

translations.literal: Gai from youth was orphaned and poor; with elder brother Zhao and younger brother Qia he was all known; he first took office as Left Attendant-in-Ordinary of a princely state.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from youth, Gai was known along with his brothers Zhao and Qia; he began as left attendant-in-ordinary of a princely state.

sentences.zh: 樂安任昉大相賞好，恒提攜溉、洽二人，廣為聲價。

translations.literal: Ren Fang of Le'an greatly admired and favored him, always guiding Gai and Qia, and widely building their reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang of Le'an greatly favored him, always promoting Gai and Qia and building their fame.

sentences.zh: 所生母魏本寒家，悉越中之資，為二兒推奉昉。

translations.literal: Their birth mother Wei was originally of a cold household; she exhausted the family's resources in Yue to support the two sons in serving Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother Wei came from a poor family and spent the household's Yue resources supporting the two sons in Fang's circle.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，昉出守義興，要溉、洽之郡，為山澤之遊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang's Tianjian, when Fang went out as Administrator of Yixing, he asked Gai and Qia to his commandery for excursions among hills and waters.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianjian's start, when Fang went out as administrator of Yixing, he took Gai and Qia to his commandery for mountain and river outings.

sentences.zh: 昉還為御史中丞，後進皆宗之。

translations.literal: When Fang returned as Censor-in-Chief, the rising generation all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang returned as censor-in-chief, younger men all looked to him as model.

sentences.zh: 時有彭城劉孝綽、劉苞、劉孺，吳郡陸倕、張率，陳郡殷芸，沛國劉顯及溉、洽，車軌日至，號曰蘭台聚。

translations.literal: At the time there were Liu Xiaochuo, Liu Bao, and Liu Ru of Pengcheng; Lu Chou and Zhang Shuai of Wu Commandery; Yin Yun of Chen Commandery; Liu Xian of Pei; and Gai and Qia—their carriages came daily, called the Orchid Terrace Gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Then came daily the carriages of Liu Xiaochuo, Liu Bao, Liu Ru, Lu Chou, Zhang Shuai, Yin Yun, Liu Xian, Gai, and Qia—the Orchid Terrace Gathering.

sentences.zh: 陸倕贈昉詩云：「和風雜美氣，下有真人游，壯矣荀文若，賢哉陳太丘。

translations.literal: Lu Chou presented Fang a poem saying, "Harmonious wind mingles with fine air; below walks the perfected man. Grand was Xun Wenruo, worthy Chen Taqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chou sent Fang a poem: "A harmonious wind mingles with noble air; below walks the perfected man. Grand was Xun Wenruo, worthy Chen Taqiu."

sentences.zh: 今則蘭台聚，方古信為儔。

translations.literal: Now the Orchid Terrace gathers—compared with antiquity, truly peers."
translations.idiomatic: "Now the Orchid Terrace gathers—peers of the ancients indeed."

sentences.zh: 任君本達識，張子復清修，既有絕塵到，復見黃中劉。

translations.literal: Ren Jun truly comprehended, Zhang Zi again refined—already there is dust-surpassing Dao, and again one sees Liu Huangzhong."
translations.idiomatic: "Ren Jun truly comprehends; Zhang Zi is refined again—already Dao surpasses the dust, and again one sees Liu Huangzhong."

sentences.zh: 」時謂昉為任君，比漢之三君，到則溉兄弟也。

translations.literal: At the time they called Fang Ren Jun, comparing him to the Three Lords of Han; Dao meant the Gai brothers.
translations.idiomatic: They called Fang "Ren Jun," likening him to Han's Three Lords; "Dao" meant the Gai brothers.

sentences.zh: 除尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Master of Writing, Hall Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Master of Writing, Hall Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後為建安太守，昉以詩贈之，求二衫段云：「鐵錢兩當一，百代易名實，為惠當及時，無待涼秋日。

translations.literal: Later he was Administrator of Jian'an; Fang presented him a poem asking for two spans of double-layered cloth, saying, "Iron cash two for one—names and substance change through the ages; as favor one should act in season, not wait for cool autumn days."
translations.idiomatic: Later as administrator of Jian'an, Fang sent a poem asking for two spans of double cloth: "Iron cash trades two for one—names and substance shift through ages. Favor should come in season, not wait for autumn's chill."

sentences.zh: 」溉答云：「餘衣本百結，閩中徒八蠶，假令金如粟，詎使廉夫貪。

translations.literal: Gai replied, "My remaining clothes were already patched; in Min only eight silkworms—suppose gold were like millet, how could an honest man be greedy?"
translations.idiomatic: Gai replied: "My clothes were already patched; in Min only eight silkworms. Even if gold were grain, an honest man would not be greedy."

sentences.zh: 」還為太子中舍人。

translations.literal: On return he was Palace Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: On return he became palace cadet.

sentences.zh: 溉長八尺，眉目如點，白皙美須髯，舉動風華，善於應答。

translations.literal: Gai was eight feet tall; eyebrows and eyes like dots; fair skin and fine beard; his bearing was elegant and he was skilled at reply.
translations.idiomatic: Gai stood eight feet; brows and eyes like painted dots; fair-skinned with a fine beard; graceful in bearing and quick in reply.

sentences.zh: 上用為通事舍人，中書郎，兼吏部，太子中庶子。

translations.literal: The Emperor used him as Master of Communications, Master of Writing, concurrent Master of the Ministry of Personnel, and Palace Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made him master of communications, master of writing, concurrent master of personnel, and palace supervisor.

sentences.zh: 湘東王繹為會稽太守，以溉為輕車長史，行府郡事。

translations.literal: When Prince of Xiangdong Liu Yi was Administrator of Kuaiji, Gai was Chief Clerk of the Light Chariots, acting in the prince's prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Xiangdong Liu Yi governed Kuaiji, Gai was chief clerk of light chariots and ran the prince's prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 武帝敕繹曰：「到溉非直為汝行事，足為汝師。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Yi, "Dao Gai is not merely to act for you—he is fully fit to be your teacher."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Yi: "Dao Gai is not merely to run your affairs—he is fit to be your teacher."

sentences.zh: 」溉嘗夢武帝遍見諸子，至湘東而脫帽與之，於是密敬事焉。

translations.literal: Gai once dreamed the Emperor visited all the princes; reaching Xiangdong he removed his cap and gave it to him; thereafter he secretly honored and served him.
translations.idiomatic: Gai dreamed the Emperor visited his sons; reaching Xiangdong he took off his cap and gave it to him. Thereafter he secretly devoted himself to the prince.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: When his mother died he observed mourning with full rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned with full rites.

sentences.zh: 所處廬開方四尺，毀瘠過人。

translations.literal: The hut he dwelt in opened four feet square; his emaciation exceeded others.
translations.idiomatic: His mourning hut measured four feet square; he wasted away beyond others.

sentences.zh: 服闋，猶蔬食布衣者累載。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he still ate vegetables and wore cloth for years.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he still ate vegetables and wore plain cloth for years.

sentences.zh: 曆御史中丞，都官、左戶二尚書，掌吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He successively served as Censor-in-Chief and Master of the Ministries of Punishments and Left Household, holding the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He served as censor-in-chief, master of punishments and left household, and held the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 時何敬容以令參選，事有不允，溉輒相執。

translations.literal: At the time He Jingrong participated in selection; when matters were not approved Gai always opposed him.
translations.idiomatic: When He Jingrong handled appointments and matters went awry, Gai always opposed him.

sentences.zh: 敬容謂人曰：「到溉尚有餘臭，遂學作貴人。

translations.literal: Jingrong said to others, "Dao Gai still has leftover stink and has learned to play the noble."
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong said: "Dao Gai still reeks of the dung-basket and plays at being gentry."

sentences.zh: 」敬容日方貴寵，人皆下之，溉忤之如初。

translations.literal: Jingrong was then newly honored and favored; all bowed to him; Gai opposed him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong was newly favored and all deferred; Gai opposed him as before.

sentences.zh: 溉祖彥之初以擔糞自給，故世以為譏云。

translations.literal: Gai's grandfather Yanzhi in the beginning supported himself by carrying night soil—so the age took it as mockery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanzhi had once carried night soil for a living—so men mocked him.

sentences.zh: 後省門鴟尾被震，溉左遷光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later the phoenix-tail finial of the ministry gate was struck by lightning; Gai was demoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Later lightning struck the ministry gate's phoenix-tail finial; Gai was demoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 所蒞以清白自修，性又率儉，不好聲色，虛室單床，傍無姬侍。

translations.literal: In every post he cultivated himself in purity; his nature was also plain and frugal; he did not love sound and color; his empty room had a single bed and no concubines at his side.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he kept himself pure; plain and frugal by nature, he cared nothing for music or women—an empty room, one bed, no concubines.

sentences.zh: 冠履十年一易，朝服或至穿補，傳呼清路，示有朝章而已。

translations.literal: Cap and shoes he changed once in ten years; court dress he sometimes wore patched through; heralds clearing the road showed only that he still had court insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He changed cap and shoes once in ten years; court robes he sometimes wore patched; heralds clearing the road showed court rank and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 後為散騎常侍、侍中、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Later he was Palace Attendant, Attendant Within, and Chancellor of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was palace attendant, attendant within, and chancellor of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 表求列武帝所撰正言於學，請置正言助教二人，學生二十人。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that the Emperor's Correct Speech be listed in the academy and that two assistant teachers of Correct Speech and twenty students be set up.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that the Emperor's Correct Speech be taught in the academy, with two assistant teachers and twenty students.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞賀琛又請加置博士一人。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Master of Writing He Chen also asked to add one erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant He Chen also asked for an additional erudite.

sentences.zh: 溉特被武帝賞接，每與對棋，從夕達旦。

translations.literal: Gai was especially favored and received by the Emperor; each time they played go together from evening till dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was especially favored; he and the Emperor played go from dusk till dawn.

sentences.zh: 或復失寢，加以低睡，帝詩嘲之曰：「狀若喪家狗，又似懸風槌。

translations.literal: Sometimes he again lost sleep and nodded off; the Emperor mocked him in verse, "Like a dog of a bereaved house, and again like a wind-beaten pestle."
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he dozed off; the Emperor mocked him in verse: "Like a bereaved house's dog, like a wind-beaten pestle."

sentences.zh: 」當時以為笑樂。

translations.literal: At the time it was taken as laughter and delight.
translations.idiomatic: Men took it as a jest.

sentences.zh: 溉第居近淮水，齋前山池有奇礓石，長一丈六尺，帝戲與賭之，並禮記一部，溉並輸焉。

translations.literal: Gai's residence lay near the Huai; before his study in hill and pool was a strange rock a zhang and six feet long; the Emperor in jest wagered it against one copy of the Book of Rites; Gai lost both.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's house stood near the Huai; before his study pool lay a strange rock sixteen feet long. The Emperor wagered it against a copy of the Book of Rites; Gai lost both.

sentences.zh: 未進，帝謂朱異曰：「卿謂到溉所輸可以送未？

translations.literal: Before it was delivered the Emperor said to Zhu Yi, "Do you think what Dao Gai lost can be sent yet?"
translations.idiomatic: Before delivery the Emperor asked Zhu Yi: "Can what Dao Gai lost be sent yet?"

sentences.zh: 」斂板對曰：「臣既事君，安敢失禮。

translations.literal: Yi folded his tablet and replied, "Your servant having served my lord, how dare I fail in ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi folded his tablet: "Having served my lord, how dare I fail in ritual?"

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑，其見親愛如此。

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed greatly; such was his intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed heartily—such was his affection.

sentences.zh: 石即迎置華林園宴殿前。

translations.literal: The stone was at once welcomed and placed before the feast hall in Huaglin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: The stone was brought at once and set before the feast hall in Huaglin Garden.

sentences.zh: 移石之日，都下傾城縱觀，所謂到公石也。

translations.literal: On the day the stone was moved the capital turned out to watch; it was called Duke Dao's Stone.
translations.idiomatic: When the stone moved the capital turned out to watch—the Duke Dao Stone.

sentences.zh: 溉弈棋入第六品，常與朱異、韋黯於御坐校棋比勢，復局不差一道。

translations.literal: Gai's go ranked sixth grade; he often matched with Zhu Yi and Wei An at the imperial seat, replaying without a single move's difference.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's go ranked sixth grade; with Zhu Yi and Wei An at the imperial seat he replayed games without a single move's error.

sentences.zh: 後因疾失明，詔以金紫光祿大夫、散騎常侍就第養疾。

translations.literal: Later because of illness he lost his sight; an edict made him Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and Palace Attendant to convalesce at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later blindness ended his sight; he was made Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and palace attendant to convalesce at home.

sentences.zh: 溉少有美名，遂不為僕射，人為之恨，溉澹如也。

translations.literal: Gai from youth had a fine name; he never became Vice Director—men resented it for him, but Gai was untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had a fine name yet never reached vice director—men regretted it; Gai was untroubled.

sentences.zh: 家門雍睦，兄弟特相友愛，初與弟洽恒共居一齋，洽卒後，便舍為寺。

translations.literal: The household was harmonious; the brothers especially loved one another; at first Gai and his younger brother Qia always shared one room; after Qia died he converted it into a temple.
translations.idiomatic: The household was harmonious; the brothers especially close. Gai and Qia had shared one room; after Qia died he made it a temple.

sentences.zh: 蔣山有延賢寺，溉家世所立。

translations.literal: On Mount Jiang was Yanxian Temple, established by Gai's family through the generations.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Jiang stood Yanxian Temple, founded by Gai's family for generations.

sentences.zh: 溉得祿俸，皆充二寺。

translations.literal: Gai's salary he devoted entirely to the two temples.
translations.idiomatic: He gave all his salary to the two temples.

sentences.zh: 因斷腥膻，終身蔬食。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cut off flesh and fish and for life ate vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: He gave up meat and fish and ate vegetables for life.

sentences.zh: 別營小室，朝夕從僧徒禮誦。

translations.literal: He set up a small room apart and morning and evening joined the monks in ritual recitation.
translations.idiomatic: He built a small room and morning and evening joined monks in recitation.

sentences.zh: 武帝每月三致淨饌，恩禮甚篤。

translations.literal: Three times each month the Emperor sent pure food; his grace and courtesy were very deep.
translations.idiomatic: Three times a month the Emperor sent pure food; his grace ran deep.

sentences.zh: 性不好交遊，唯與朱異、劉之遴、張綰同志友密。

translations.literal: By nature he did not love socializing; only Zhu Yi, Liu Zhilin, and Zhang Chuo were close friends of one mind.
translations.idiomatic: He did not love society; only Zhu Yi, Liu Zhilin, and Zhang Chuo were intimate friends.

sentences.zh: 及臥疾，門可羅雀，唯三人每歲時恒鳴騶枉道以相存問，置酒極歡而去。

translations.literal: When he lay ill sparrows could be netted at the gate; only the three men each year at the seasons always came with outriders by a detour to inquire, set wine, and leave in utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: When ill, sparrows could be netted at his gate; only those three each season came by detour with outriders, drank, and left in joy.

sentences.zh: 乙太清二年卒，臨終托張、劉勒子孫薄葬之禮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiqing he died; at the end he entrusted Zhang and Liu to admonish his sons and grandsons in the rites of simple burial.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing year two he died; at the end he asked Zhang and Liu to admonish his heirs in simple burial.

sentences.zh: 曰：「氣絕便斂，斂以法服，先有塚竁，斂竟便葬，不須擇日。

translations.literal: He said, "When breath ends, wrap at once; wrap in lawful garments; a tomb niche already exists—when wrapping is done, bury at once; no need to choose a day.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "When breath ends, wrap at once in lawful garments. The tomb niche is ready—bury when wrapping is done; no need to choose a day.

sentences.zh: 凶事必存約儉，孫侄不得違言。

translations.literal: Mourning affairs must keep to simplicity and frugality; sons and nephews must not disobey these words."
translations.idiomatic: Keep mourning simple; sons and nephews must not disobey."

sentences.zh: 」便屏家人請僧讀經贊唄，及卒，顏色如恒，手屈二指，即佛道所雲得果也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent away his family and asked monks to read sutras and chant praises; when he died his color was as usual; his hand bent two fingers—the fruit the Buddha Way speaks of attaining.
translations.idiomatic: He dismissed his family and had monks read sutras. At death his color was unchanged; two fingers bent—the Buddha's promised fruit.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷多事，遂無贈諡。

translations.literal: At the time the court had many affairs; thus there was no posthumous enfeoffment or title.
translations.idiomatic: The court was busy; he received no posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷行于時。

translations.literal: He had a collection of twenty juan circulating in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty juan of his writings circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 子鏡。

translations.literal: His son Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jing.

sentences.zh: 鏡字圓照，初在孕，其母夢懷鏡，及生，因以名焉。

translations.literal: Jing, courtesy name Yuanzhao—in the womb his mother dreamed she carried a mirror; when he was born, therefore, he was so named.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, styled Yuanzhao: while in the womb his mother dreamed she carried a mirror, and so named him.

sentences.zh: 鏡五歲便口授為詩，婉有辭況。

translations.literal: At five Jing could orally compose poetry; his phrasing was graceful.
translations.idiomatic: At five he could compose poetry by mouth; his phrasing was graceful.

sentences.zh: 位太子舍人，作七悟文甚美，先溉卒。

translations.literal: He held the post of Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent; his Seven Awakenings essay was very fine; he died before Gai.
translations.idiomatic: He was palace attendant to the heir; his Seven Awakenings essay was fine; he died before Gai.

sentences.zh: 鏡子藎，早聰慧，位尚書殿中郎，嘗從武帝幸京口，登北顧樓賦詩。

translations.literal: Jing's son Jin was clever early and held the post of Master of Writing, Hall Attendant; he once followed the Emperor to Jingkou and ascended Beigu Tower to compose a poem.
translations.idiomatic: Jing's son Jin was clever early and served as Master of Writing, Hall Attendant; once at Jingkou he climbed Beigu Tower and composed a poem at the Emperor's order.

sentences.zh: 藎受詔便就，上以示溉曰：「藎定是才子，翻恐卿從來文章假手於藎。

translations.literal: Jin received the edict and composed on the spot; the Emperor showed it to Gai and said, "Jin is surely a talent; I fear your writings have always been ghostwritten by Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Jin composed on the spot; the Emperor showed Gai the piece: "Jin is surely a talent—I fear your essays have been Jin's work all along."

sentences.zh: 」因賜絹二十疋。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He gave twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 後溉每和禦詩，上輒手詔戲溉曰：「得無貽厥之力乎？

translations.literal: Later whenever Gai matched the Emperor's poems, the Emperor would personally write in jest to Gai, "Surely this is not the strength of leaving a legacy?"
translations.idiomatic: Later when Gai matched imperial poems the Emperor jested by hand: "Not the strength of leaving a legacy, surely?"

sentences.zh: 」又賜溉連珠曰：「硯磨墨以騰文，筆飛毫以書信，如飛蛾之赴火，豈焚身之可吝。

translations.literal: He again bestowed on Gai a linked pearl saying, "The ink-slab grinds ink to soar in pattern; the brush flies bristles to write letters—like moths rushing fire, how can one regret the burning body?
translations.idiomatic: He sent Gai a linked pearl: "The slab grinds ink to soar in pattern; the brush flies to write—like moths to flame, who regrets the burning body?

sentences.zh: 必耄年其已及，可假之於少藎。

translations.literal: When old age surely comes, one may borrow from young Jin."
translations.idiomatic: When old age comes, borrow from young Jin."

sentences.zh: 」其見知賞如此。

translations.literal: Such was the knowing favor he received.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor he enjoyed.

sentences.zh: 後除丹陽尹丞。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Assistant Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was assistant administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 太清亂，赴江陵卒。

translations.literal: In the Taiqing disorders he went to Jiangling and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taiqing disorders he went to Jiangling and died there.

sentences.zh: 溉弟洽。

translations.literal: Gai's younger brother Qia.
translations.idiomatic: Gai's younger brother was Qia.

sentences.zh: 洽字茂沿，清警有才學。

translations.literal: Qia, courtesy name Maoyan, was clear and alert with talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Qia, styled Maoyan, was clear-minded, talented, and learned.

sentences.zh: 父坦以洽無外家，乃求娶于羊玄保以為外氏。

translations.literal: His father Tan, because Qia had no maternal kin, sought a marriage with Yang Xuanbao to serve as maternal relatives.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan, since Qia had no maternal kin, arranged a marriage with Yang Xuanbao's house as maternal family.

sentences.zh: 洽年十八，為徐州迎西曹行事。

translations.literal: At eighteen Qia was Acting Western Bureau Officer receiving Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was acting western bureau officer for Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 謝朓文章盛于一時，見洽深相賞好，每稱其兼資文武。

translations.literal: Xie Tiao's writings flourished for a time; seeing Qia he deeply admired and favored him and often praised his combined civil and military endowment.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiao's writing ruled the age; he deeply favored Qia and often praised his civil and military gifts together.

sentences.zh: 朓後為吏部，欲薦之，洽睹時方亂，深相拒絕，遂築室岩阿，幽居積歲，時人號曰居士。

translations.literal: Later Tiao was in the Ministry of Personnel and wished to recommend him; Qia saw the times turning chaotic and firmly refused, then built a dwelling in rocky hills and lived secluded for years; men of the time called him the Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiao ran personnel he wished to recommend Qia; Qia saw chaos coming, refused firmly, built in the hills, and lived secluded for years—men called him the Recluse.

sentences.zh: 任昉與洽兄沼、溉並善，嘗訪洽于田舍，歎曰：「此子日下無雙。

translations.literal: Ren Fang was on good terms with Qia's elder brothers Zhao and Gai and once visited Qia at his farmstead, sighing, "This son under heaven has no peer."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fang, friend to Qia's brothers Zhao and Gai, visited Qia at his farm and sighed: "Under heaven this man has no peer."

sentences.zh: 」遂申拜親之禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he extended the rites of treating him as kin.
translations.idiomatic: He then treated Qia as kin.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝嘗問待詔丘遲曰：「到洽何如沆溉？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang once asked the awaiting-edict Qiu Chi, "How does Dao Qia compare with Hang and Gai?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once asked awaiting-edict Qiu Chi: "How does Dao Qia compare with Hang and Gai?"

sentences.zh: 」遲曰：「正情過於沆，文章不減溉；

translations.literal: Chi said, "In upright feeling he surpasses Hang; in writing he does not fall below Gai;"
translations.idiomatic: Chi said: "In upright feeling he surpasses Hang; in writing he does not fall below Gai;"

sentences.zh: 加以清言，殆將難及。

translations.literal: add sincerity in pure talk—perhaps nearly impossible to match.
translations.idiomatic: add pure conversation—perhaps nearly impossible to match."

sentences.zh: 」即召為太子舍人。

translations.literal: He was at once summoned as Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned at once as palace attendant to the heir.

sentences.zh: 禦幸華光殿，詔洽及沆、蕭琛、任昉侍宴，賦二十韻詩，以洽辭為工，賜絹二十疋。

translations.literal: On an imperial visit to Huaguang Hall the Emperor ordered Qia with Hang, Xiao Chen, and Ren Fang to attend the feast and compose twenty-rhyme poems; Qia's wording was judged the finest and he was given twenty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: At Huaguang Hall the Emperor ordered Qia, Hang, Xiao Chen, and Ren Fang to feast and compose twenty-rhyme poems; Qia's was judged finest and he received twenty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 上謂昉曰：「諸到可謂才子。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Fang, "The Dao clan can be called talents."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Fang: "The Dao clan are true talents."

sentences.zh: 昉曰：「臣常竊議，宋得其武，梁得其文。

translations.literal: Fang said, "Your servant has often privately judged: Song got their martial, Liang got their literary."
translations.idiomatic: Fang said: "I have often said: Song got their martial, Liang their literary."

sentences.zh: 」遷司徒主簿，直待詔省，敕使抄甲部書為十二卷。

translations.literal: He was moved to Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, direct in the awaiting-edicts office; an edict had him copy the A section of books into twelve juan.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief clerk of the Minister of Education, direct in the awaiting-edicts office, and copied the A section of books into twelve juan.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Master of Writing, Hall Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Master of Writing, Hall Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後為太子中舍人，與庶子陸倕對掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: Later he was Palace Cadet and with the Supervisor Lu Chou paired in managing Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: Later as palace cadet he paired with Supervisor Lu Chou in managing Eastern Palace records.

sentences.zh: 俄為侍讀，侍讀省仍置學士二人，洽充其選。

translations.literal: Soon he was Reader; the Readers' Office still set up two scholars, and Qia filled one selection.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reader; the Readers' Office set two scholars and Qia filled one.

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士，奉敕撰太學碑。

translations.literal: He was moved to Erudite of the Imperial University and received command to compose the Imperial Academy stele.
translations.idiomatic: He became erudite of the Imperial University and received command to compose the academy stele.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書吏部郎，請托不行。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Master of Writing, Ministry of Personnel Lang, and would not act on entreaties.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Master of Writing in personnel, he refused entreaties.

sentences.zh: 徙左丞，準繩不避貴戚。

translations.literal: Moved to Left Assistant, he measured by the standard and did not avoid the noble and kin.
translations.idiomatic: As left assistant he held to the standard and did not spare noble kin.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲親戎，軍國禮容多自洽出。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor wished to lead the army in person; much military and state ritual came from Qia.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor wished to lead in person, much military and state ritual came from Qia.

sentences.zh: 尋遷御史中丞，號為勁直。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Censor-in-Chief and was called forceful and upright.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was censor-in-chief, called forceful and upright.

sentences.zh: 少與劉孝綽善，下車便以名教隱穢，首彈之。

translations.literal: From youth he was on good terms with Liu Xiaochuo; on taking office he used name-and-teaching to conceal filth and impeached him first.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was friends with Liu Xiaochuo; on taking office he impeached him first for moral failings under cover of teaching.

sentences.zh: 孝綽托與諸弟書，實欲聞之湘東王。

translations.literal: Xiaochuo entrusted a letter to his brothers but in fact wished Xiangdong Wang to hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaochuo sent a letter to his brothers but meant Prince of Xiangdong to hear.

sentences.zh: 公事左降，猶居職。

translations.literal: For the public matter he was demoted to the left but still held office.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted for the affair, he still held office.

sentences.zh: 舊制中丞不得入尚書下舍，洽兄溉為左戶尚書，洽引服親不應有礙，刺省詳決。

translations.literal: By old rule the censor-in-chief might not enter the Masters of Writing's lower quarters; Qia's elder brother Gai was Master of the Left Household; Qia cited mourning garb kin and that there should be no obstruction, and memorialized the ministry for detailed decision.
translations.idiomatic: By old rule the censor might not enter the Masters of Writing's lower quarters; Gai was Master of the Left Household; Qia cited mourning kin and memorialized for decision.

sentences.zh: 左丞蕭子雲議許入溉省，亦以其兄弟素篤不相別也。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Xiao Ziyun judged permission to enter Gai's office, also because the brothers from of old were deeply devoted and did not separate.
translations.idiomatic: Left Assistant Xiao Ziyun allowed entry to Gai's office, since the brothers were devoted and did not stand apart.

sentences.zh: 出為尋陽太守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as administrator of Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈侍中，諡理子。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously Attendant Within; posthumous title Li-zi.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously made Attendant Within with posthumous title Li-zi.

sentences.zh: 洽美容質，善言吐，弱年聽伏曼容講，未嘗傍膝，伏深歎之。

translations.literal: Qia had fine looks and was skilled in speech; in weak years he heard Fu Manrong lecture and never sat on the side of the knee; Fu deeply admired this.
translations.idiomatic: Qia was handsome and eloquent; as a boy hearing Fu Manrong lecture he never sat casually; Fu admired this deeply.

sentences.zh: 文集行於世。

translations.literal: His collected writings circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated.

sentences.zh: 子仲舉。

translations.literal: His son Zhongju.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zhongju.

sentences.zh: 仲舉既無學術，朝章非其所長，選舉引用，皆出自袁樞。

translations.literal: Zhongju had no learning; court regulations were not his strength; selection and appointment all came from Yuan Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju had no learning; court rules were not his strength; appointments all came from Yuan Shu.

sentences.zh: 性疏簡，不幹時務，與朝士無所親狎，但聚財酣飲而已。

translations.literal: By nature he was careless and did not attend to affairs of the age; with court gentlemen he was not intimate; he only amassed wealth and drank deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Careless by nature, he ignored public affairs, kept no court intimates, and only hoarded wealth and drank.

sentences.zh: 文帝積年寢疾，不親萬機，尚書中書事，皆使仲舉斷決。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen for years lay ill and did not personally handle the myriad affairs; Masters of Writing and the Secretariat matters were all decided by Zhongju.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen lay ill for years and did not govern; Zhongju decided matters of the Masters of Writing and Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天康元年，遷侍中、尚書僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiankang he was moved to Attendant Within and Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiankang year one he became attendant within and vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 文帝疾甚，入侍醫藥。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's illness was severe, he entered to attend medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor's illness worsened he entered to attend his medicine.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，宣帝受遺詔為尚書令入輔，仲舉與左丞王暹、中書舍人劉師知、殷不佞，以朝望有歸，乃遣不佞宣旨遣宣帝還東府，事發，師知下獄賜死，暹、不佞並付推，乃以仲舉為貞毅將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died, Emperor Xuan received the testamentary edict as Master of Writing and entered to assist; Zhongju with Left Assistant Wang Xuan, Palace Attendant Liu Shizhi, and Yin Buniu, because court prestige had a direction, sent Buniu with an edict to dismiss Emperor Xuan back to the Eastern Palace; when the affair leaked, Shizhi was imprisoned and granted death, Xuan and Buniu were both handed to investigators, and Zhongju was made General of Zhenyì and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor died, Emperor Xuan took the testament as Master of Writing and entered to assist. Zhongju with Wang Xuan, Liu Shizhi, and Yin Buniu, trusting court prestige, sent Buniu to dismiss Xuan to the Eastern Palace. When it leaked, Shizhi was imprisoned and killed; Xuan and Buniu were investigated; Zhongju was made General of Zhenyì and Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 初，仲舉子郁尚文帝妹信義長公主，官至中書侍郎，出為宣城太守，文帝配以士馬。

translations.literal: At first Zhongju's son Yu married Emperor Wen's younger sister Princess Xin'yi, held the post of Attendant Master of Writing, went out as Administrator of Xuancheng; Emperor Wen paired him with gentry and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongju's son Yu had married Emperor Wen's sister Princess Xin'yi, served as attendant master of writing, and went out as administrator of Xuancheng with gentry and horses from the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 是年，遷南康內史，以國哀未之任。

translations.literal: That year he was moved to Administrator of Nankang; because of national mourning he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was moved to administrator of Nankang but did not take up the post for national mourning.

sentences.zh: 仲舉既廢居私宅，與鬱皆不自安。

translations.literal: Zhongju, dismissed, dwelt in his private residence; he and Yu were both ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed, Zhongju lived at home; he and Yu were both uneasy.

sentences.zh: 時韓子高在都，人馬素盛，鬱每乘小輿蒙婦人衣與子高謀。

translations.literal: At the time Han Zigao was in the capital with men and horses always strong; Yu each time rode in a small carriage wearing women's clothes to plot with Zigao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zigao then held the capital with strong forces; Yu rode in a small carriage in women's dress to plot with him.

sentences.zh: 子高軍主告其事，宣帝收子高、仲舉及郁，並於獄賜死。

translations.literal: Zigao's army commander reported the affair; Emperor Xuan seized Zigao, Zhongju, and Yu and all granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zigao's commander reported it; Emperor Xuan seized Zigao, Zhongju, and Yu and had all three killed in prison.

sentences.zh: 郁諸男女以帝甥獲免。

translations.literal: Yu's sons and daughters by the Emperor's nephew-status were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's children were spared as the Emperor's nephews and nieces.

sentences.zh: 垣護之字彥宗，略陽桓道人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Huzhi, courtesy name Yanzong, was a man of Huandao in Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Huzhi, styled Yanzong, came from Huandao in Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 族姓豪強，石季龍時，自略陽徙鄴。

translations.literal: The clan surname was powerful; in Shi Hu's time they moved from Lueyang to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The clan was powerful; under Shi Hu they moved from Lueyang to Ye.

sentences.zh: 祖敞仕苻氏，為長樂國郎中令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chang served the Fu clan as Commandant of the Principality of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chang served Former Qin as commandant of the Principality of Changle.

sentences.zh: 伯父遵、父苗仕慕容超，並見委任。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Zun and father Miao served Murong Chao and were both entrusted with office.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zun and father Miao served Murong Chao and were both trusted with office.

sentences.zh: 遵為尚書，苗為京兆太守。

translations.literal: Zun was Master of Writing; Miao was Administrator of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was Master of Writing; Miao was administrator of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝圍廣固，遵、苗踰城歸降，並以為太尉行參軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song besieged Guanggu, Zun and Miao crossed the wall to surrender and were both made Acting Aides in the Grand Commandant's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu besieged Guanggu, Zun and Miao climbed down the wall to surrender and became acting aides in the Grand Commandant's army.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，遵為員外散騎常侍，苗屯騎校尉，仍家下邳。

translations.literal: In Yuanjia, Zun was Supernumerary Palace Attendant; Miao was Colonel of Agile Cavalry; they still made their home at Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia Zun was supernumerary palace attendant; Miao was colonel of agile cavalry; the family remained at Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 護之少倜儻，不拘小節，形狀短陋而氣幹強果。

translations.literal: Huzhi from youth was free and bold, not bound by small matters; his form was short and ugly but his spirit and resolve were strong and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Huzhi was bold and heedless of small rules; short and plain in looks, yet strong and resolute in spirit.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初為殿中將軍，隨到彥之北侵魏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia he was General of the Palace and followed Dao Yanzhi north to invade Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanjia's start he was a palace general and followed Dao Yanzhi north against Wei.

sentences.zh: 彥之將回師，護之書諫，彥之不納，散敗而歸。

translations.literal: When Yanzhi was about to turn the army back, Huzhi wrote remonstrance; Yanzhi did not accept; scattered defeat and return followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhi prepared to withdraw, Huzhi wrote in protest; Yanzhi refused; defeat and rout followed.

sentences.zh: 文帝聞而善之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen heard and approved.

sentences.zh: 累遷鍾離太守，隨王玄謨入河。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Zhongli and followed Wang Xuemo into the river.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to administrator of Zhongli and followed Wang Xuemo into the river country.

sentences.zh: 玄謨攻滑台，護之百舸為前鋒，進據石濟。

translations.literal: Xuemo attacked Huatai; Huzhi with a hundred boats was vanguard and advanced to hold Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo attacked Huatai; Huzhi with a hundred boats led the van and seized Shiji.

sentences.zh: 及魏救將至，馳書勸玄謨急攻之，不見從。

translations.literal: When Wei's relief was about to arrive, he sent a fast letter urging Xuemo to attack urgently; he was not obeyed.
