translations.idiomatic: When Wei relief neared he urged Xuemo to attack at once; Xuemo would not listen.

sentences.zh: 玄謨敗退，不暇報護之，而魏軍悉牽玄謨水軍大艚，連以鐵鎖三重，斷河以絕護之還路。

translations.literal: Xuemo was defeated and retreated, with no time to inform Huzhi; Wei forces all towed Xuemo's great river ships, linking them with triple iron chains to cut the river and sever Huzhi's return.
translations.idiomatic: Xuemo retreated in defeat without warning Huzhi; Wei towed his great ships, chained the river in triple iron links, and cut off Huzhi's return.

sentences.zh: 河水迅急，護之中流而下，每至鐵鎖，以長柯斧斷之，魏人不能禁。

translations.literal: The river water ran swift; Huzhi went downstream; each time he reached an iron chain he used a long-shafted axe to cut it; Wei men could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: The current ran swift; Huzhi went downstream; at each iron chain he cut with a long-shafted axe; Wei could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 唯失一舸，余舸並全。

translations.literal: Only one boat was lost; the rest were all preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He lost only one boat; the rest escaped intact.

sentences.zh: 留戍麋溝城。

translations.literal: He remained to garrison Migou city.
translations.idiomatic: He remained to garrison Migou.

sentences.zh: 還為江夏王義恭驃騎戶曹參軍，戍淮陰，領濟北太守。

translations.literal: On return he was Household Aide to the Flying Cavalry of Prince of Jiangxia Liu Yigong, garrisoned Huaiyin, and held concurrent Administrator of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was household aide to Flying Cavalry Prince of Jiangxia Liu Yigong, garrisoned Huaiyin, and concurrently governed Jibei.

sentences.zh: 三十年，文帝崩，還屯曆下。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year Emperor Wen died; he returned to encamp below Li.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty Emperor Wen died; he returned to encamp below Li.

sentences.zh: 孝武入討，率所領馳赴，帝以為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered to punish the usurper, he led his command and raced to join; the Emperor made him Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu marched to punish the usurper, Huzhi raced to join with his command; the Emperor made him inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 及南郡王義宣反，兗州刺史徐遺寶，護之妻弟也，與護之書，勸使同逆。

translations.literal: When Prince of Nan Commandery Liu Yixuan rebelled, Inspector of Yanzhou Xu Yibao, Huzhi's wife's younger brother, wrote Huzhi urging him to join the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Nan Commandery Liu Yixuan rebelled, Inspector of Yanzhou Xu Yibao, Huzhi's brother-in-law, wrote urging him to join.

sentences.zh: 護之馳使以聞，率軍隨沈慶之等擊魯爽。

translations.literal: Huzhi sent a fast messenger to report and led the army following Shen Qingzhi and others to strike Lu Shuang.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi reported by fast messenger and led troops with Shen Qingzhi to strike Lu Shuang.

sentences.zh: 義宣率大眾至梁山，與王玄謨相持，柳元景率護之及護之弟詢之、柳叔仁、鄭琨等出鎮新亭，玄謨求救，上遣元景等進據南州。

translations.literal: Yixuan led the great host to Liangshan and faced Wang Xuemo; Liu Yuanjing led Huzhi and Huzhi's younger brother Xunzhi, Liu Shuren, Zheng Kun, and others out to garrison Xinting; Xuemo sought rescue and the Emperor sent Yuanjing and the rest to advance and hold South Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yixuan brought his host to Liangshan against Wang Xuemo; Liu Yuanjing led Huzhi, Xunzhi, Liu Shuren, and Zheng Kun to garrison Xinting; Xuemo called for aid and the Emperor sent Yuanjing south.

sentences.zh: 護之水軍先發，大破賊將龐法起，元景乃以精兵配護之追討，會朱修之已平江陵，至尋陽而還。

translations.literal: Huzhi's river force set out first and greatly defeated the rebel general Pang Faqi; Yuanjing then gave Huzhi picked troops to pursue; when Zhu Xiuzhi had already pacified Jiangling they reached Xunyang and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huzhi's fleet moved first and broke rebel general Pang Faqi; Yuanjing gave him elite troops to pursue; when Zhu Xiuzhi had pacified Jiangling they reached Xunyang and returned.

sentences.zh: 遷徐州刺史，封益陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He was moved to Inspector of Xuzhou and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He became inspector of Xuzhou and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 後拜青、冀二州刺史，鎮曆城。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Qing and Ji and garrisoned Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he governed Qing and Ji and garrisoned Licheng.

sentences.zh: 大明三年，徵為右衛將軍還，于道聞竟陵王誕據廣陵反，護之即率部曲受車騎大將軍沈慶之節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming he was summoned as General of the Right Guard to return; on the road he heard Prince of Jingling Liu Dan held Guangling in rebellion; Huzhi at once led his followers under the command of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry Shen Qingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In Daming year three he was recalled as General of the Right Guard; on the road he heard Prince of Jingling Liu Dan held Guangling; he at once led his men under Shen Qingzhi.

sentences.zh: 事平，轉臨淮太守，徙豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was moved to Administrator of Linhuai and transferred to Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When it was settled he became administrator of Linhuai, then inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 護之所蒞，多聚斂賄貨，七年，坐下獄免官。

translations.literal: In every post Huzhi held he amassed bribes and goods; in the seventh year he was imprisoned and removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he amassed bribes; in year seven he was imprisoned and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 明年，起為太中大夫，未拜，以憤卒。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled as Grand Master of the Palace; before accepting appointment he died of anger.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled as Grand Master of the Palace; before accepting he died of rage.

sentences.zh: 諡壯侯。

translations.literal: Posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 崇祖字敬遠，一字僧寶，護之弟子也。

translations.literal: Chongzu, courtesy name Jingyuan, alternate name Sengbao, was Huzhi's younger brother's son.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu, styled Jingyuan, also called Sengbao, was Huzhi's nephew.

sentences.zh: 父詢之，驍敢有氣力。

translations.literal: His father Xunzhi was bold and had physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xunzhi was bold and strong.

sentences.zh: 元凶弑逆，副輔國將軍張柬。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince murdered his father, he served as deputy to General Who Supports the State Zhang Dong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince murdered his father, he served under General Who Supports the State Zhang Dong.

sentences.zh: 時張超之手行大逆，亦領軍隸柬，詢之規殺之，慮柬不同，柬宿有此志，又未測詢之同否，互相觀察。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Chao-zhi's own hand had done the great crime and also commanded troops under Dong; Xunzhi plotted to kill him, fearing Dong would not agree; Dong had long had this intent yet had not measured whether Xunzhi agreed; each watched the other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao-zhi had done the great crime and also commanded troops under Dong; Xunzhi plotted to kill him but feared Dong would disagree; Dong had long wished it yet had not tested Xunzhi; each watched the other.

sentences.zh: 會超之來論事，柬色動，詢之覺之，即共定謀，遣召超之。

translations.literal: When Chao-zhi came to discuss affairs, Dong's color changed; Xunzhi noticed and together they fixed the plan, sending to summon Chao-zhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao-zhi came to discuss affairs Dong's face changed; Xunzhi noticed; together they fixed the plan and summoned Chao-zhi.

sentences.zh: 超之疑之不至，改宿他所，詢之不知，徑往斫之，殺其僕於床，因與柬南奔。

translations.literal: Chao-zhi suspected and did not come, changing lodging elsewhere; Xunzhi did not know, went straight to hack him, killed his servant on the bed, then fled south with Dong.
translations.idiomatic: Chao-zhi suspected and stayed elsewhere; Xunzhi did not know, went straight to strike, killed a servant in the bed, then fled south with Dong.

sentences.zh: 時孝武已即位，以為積射將軍。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Xiaowu had already ascended; he was made General of Strong Crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu had already ascended; he was made General of Strong Crossbows.

sentences.zh: 梁山之役，力戰中流矢卒，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Liangshan campaign he fought hard, took a flying arrow midstream, and died; posthumously Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Liangshan he fought hard, took an arrow midstream, and died; posthumously inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇祖年十四，有幹略，伯父護之謂門宗曰：「此兒必大吾門。

translations.literal: Chongzu at fourteen had capacity and plan; his uncle Huzhi told the clan, "This boy will greatly enlarge our house."
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen Chongzu had capacity and plan; Huzhi told the clan: "This boy will greatly enlarge our house."

sentences.zh: 」後隨徐州刺史薛安都入魏。

translations.literal: Later he followed Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu into Wei.

sentences.zh: 尋又率門宗據朐山歸宋，求淮北立功，明帝以為北琅邪、蘭陵二郡太守，封下邳子。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he led the clan to hold Qushan and return to Song, seeking merit north of the Huai; Emperor Ming made him Administrator of North Langya and Lanling and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he led the clan to hold Qushan and return to Song, seeking merit north of the Huai; Emperor Ming made him administrator of North Langya and Lanling and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 及齊高帝鎮淮陰，崇祖時戍朐山，既受都督，祗奉甚至，帝以其武勇，善待之，崇祖謂其妹夫皇甫肅曰：「此真吾君也「，遂密佈誠節。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi garrisoned Huaiyin, Chongzu then garrisoned Qushan; having received overall command, his reverent service was utmost; the Emperor because of his martial courage treated him well; Chongzu told his brother-in-law Huangfu Su, "This is truly my lord," and thereupon secretly pledged loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Gaozu garrisoned Huaiyin, Chongzu garrisoned Qushan; under overall command he served with utmost reverence; the Emperor favored his courage; Chongzu told his brother-in-law Huangfu Su: "This is truly my lord," and secretly pledged loyalty.

sentences.zh: 高帝威名已著，宋明帝尤所忌疾，徵為黃門郎，規害高帝，崇祖建策以免，由是甚見親，參豫密謀。

translations.literal: Gaozu's authority and name were already established; Emperor Ming of Song especially hated and feared him, summoned him as Attendant Within the Yellow Gate, and plotted to harm Gaozu; Chongzu devised a plan to escape harm; by this he was greatly trusted and joined secret counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's fame was established; Emperor Ming especially feared him, summoned him as Attendant Within, and plotted harm; Chongzu devised escape; by this he was deeply trusted in secret counsel.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，高帝懼禍，令崇祖入魏。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui Gaozu feared disaster and ordered Chongzu into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanhui's end Gaozu feared disaster and sent Chongzu into Wei.

sentences.zh: 崇祖即以家口托皇甫肅，勒數百人將入魏界，更聽後旨，會蒼梧廢，召崇祖還都。

translations.literal: Chongzu at once entrusted his household to Huangfu Su, led several hundred men about to enter Wei territory, and waited further orders; when Cangwu was deposed he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted his household to Huangfu Su, led several hundred men toward Wei, and waited orders; when Cangwu was deposed he was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及齊高帝新踐阼，恐魏致討，以送劉昶為辭。

translations.literal: When Gaozu had newly ascended the throne he feared Wei would raise punishment and used sending Liu Chang as pretext.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu newly ascended he feared Wei would attack and used sending Liu Chang as pretext.

sentences.zh: 以為軍沖必在壽春，非崇祖莫可為捍，徙為豫州刺史、監豫、司二州諸軍事，封望蔡侯。

translations.literal: He judged the military thrust must be at Shouyang and none but Chongzu could defend; he moved him to Inspector of Yuzhou, overseeing Yuzhou and Sizhou military affairs, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wangcai.
translations.idiomatic: He judged the thrust must fall on Shouyang and only Chongzu could defend; he made him inspector of Yuzhou, overseeing Yuzhou and Sizhou, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Wangcai.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，魏遣劉昶攻壽春，崇祖乃於城西北立堰塞肥水，堰北起小城，使數千人守之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan Wei sent Liu Chang to attack Shouyang; Chongzu then on the northwest of the city built a dam to block the Fei River; north of the dam he raised a small city and set several thousand men to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan year two Wei sent Liu Chang against Shouyang; Chongzu built a dam northwest of the city to block the Fei, raised a small city north of it, and set several thousand men to hold it.

sentences.zh: 謂長史封延伯曰：「虜必悉力攻小城，若破此堰，放水一激，急逾三峽，自然沈溺，豈非小勞而大利邪？

translations.literal: He told Chief Clerk Feng Yanbo, "The barbarians will surely exert all strength on the small city; if this dam is broken and water released in one rush, rushing past Three Gorges, they will naturally drown—is this not small labor for great profit?"
translations.idiomatic: He told Chief Clerk Feng Yanbo: "The enemy will throw all strength at the small city; break the dam and one rush of water through the gorges will drown them—is that not small labor for great gain?"

sentences.zh: 」及魏軍由西道集堰南，分軍東路，肉薄攻小城，崇祖著白紗帽，肩輿上城，手自轉式，日晡時，決小史埭，水勢奔下，魏攻城之眾，溺死千數，大眾退走。

translations.literal: When Wei forces gathered south of the dam by the western road and divided an eastern route, pressing flesh-close to attack the small city, Chongzu wore a white gauze cap, rode in a shoulder litter up the wall, and turned the sluice-gate himself; at the hour of shen the small official dam was opened; water rushed down; of Wei's besiegers thousands drowned; the great host retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Wei gathered south of the dam, split an eastern force, and pressed the small city at close quarters. Chongzu in a white gauze cap rode a litter to the wall and opened the sluice himself; at dusk the dam broke; thousands drowned; the host retreated.

sentences.zh: 初，崇祖于淮陰見高帝，便自比韓、白，唯上獨許之。

translations.literal: At first when Chongzu saw Gaozu at Huaiyin he compared himself to Han Xin and Bai Qi; only the Emperor alone approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzu first met Gaozu at Huaiyin he compared himself to Han Xin and Bai Qi; only the Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 及破魏軍啟至，上謂朝臣曰：「崇祖恒自擬韓、白，今真其人也。

translations.literal: When the report of breaking Wei forces arrived the Emperor said to the court ministers, "Chongzu always likened himself to Han and Bai—now he truly is such a man."
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory came the Emperor told the court: "Chongzu always likened himself to Han and Bai—now he truly is."

sentences.zh: 」進為都督。

translations.literal: He was advanced to overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to overall command.

sentences.zh: 崇祖聞陳顯達、李安人皆增給軍儀，乃啟求鼓吹橫吹。

translations.literal: Chongzu heard Chen Xianda and Li Anren were both given additional military insignia and memorialized asking for drums and transverse flutes.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Chen Xianda and Li Anren had received added military insignia, he asked for drums and transverse flutes.

sentences.zh: 上敕曰：「韓、白何可不與眾異。

translations.literal: The Emperor's command said, "Han and Bai—how could they not differ from the multitude?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wrote: "Han and Bai—how should they not differ from the multitude?"

sentences.zh: 」給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He was given one set of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: He received one set of drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 崇祖慮魏復攻淮北，啟徙下蔡戍於淮東。

translations.literal: Chongzu feared Wei would again attack north of the Huai and memorialized moving the Xiapi garrison to the east of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Wei would attack north of the Huai again, he asked to move the Xiapi garrison east of the river.

sentences.zh: 其冬，魏果欲攻下蔡，及聞內徙，乃揚聲平除故城。

translations.literal: That winter Wei indeed wished to attack Xiapi; hearing of the inward move they proclaimed leveling the old city.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Wei meant to attack Xiapi; hearing of the move inland they proclaimed they would level the old city.

sentences.zh: 眾疑魏當於故城立戍，崇祖曰：「下蔡去鎮咫尺，魏豈敢置戍，實是欲除此城，正恐奔走，殺之不盡耳。

translations.literal: The multitude suspected Wei would set a garrison at the old city; Chongzu said, "Xiapi is a hand's breadth from the seat of command—how would Wei dare set a garrison? In truth they mean to destroy this city; I only fear they flee and we cannot kill them all."
translations.idiomatic: Men suspected Wei would garrison the old city; Chongzu said: "Xiapi is a hand's breadth from headquarters—Wei would not dare garrison it. They mean to raze the city; I only fear they flee before we can kill them all."

sentences.zh: 」魏果夷掘下蔡城，崇祖大破之。

translations.literal: Wei indeed razed and dug up Xiapi city; Chongzu greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei razed Xiapi; Chongzu routed them.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，為五兵尚書，領驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended he was Master of the Five Armies and concurrent General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended he was Master of the Five Armies and concurrent General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初，豫章王有盛寵，武帝在東宮，崇祖不自附。

translations.literal: At first Prince of Yuzhang enjoyed great favor; Emperor Wu in the Eastern Palace—Chongzu did not attach himself.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang once enjoyed great favor; Emperor Wu in the Eastern Palace—Chongzu did not attach himself.

sentences.zh: 及破魏軍，詔使還朝，與共密議，武帝疑之，曲加禮待。

translations.literal: When Wei forces were broken an edict had him return to court for secret counsel together; Emperor Wu suspected him and treated him with strained courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After breaking Wei an edict recalled him for secret counsel; Emperor Wu suspected him and treated him with strained courtesy.

sentences.zh: 酒後謂曰：「世間流言，我已豁懷抱，自今已後，富貴見付也。

translations.literal: After wine he said to him, "Rumors in the world—I have already opened my breast; from now on wealth and honor are entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: After wine he said: "I have set aside the world's rumors; from now on wealth and honor are yours."

sentences.zh: 」崇祖拜謝。

translations.literal: Chongzu bowed in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu bowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 及去後，高帝復遣荀伯玉敕以邊事，受旨夜發，不得辭東宮，武帝以為不盡誠心，銜之。

translations.literal: After he left Gaozu again sent Xun Boyu with command on border affairs; receiving orders he set out by night and could not bid the Eastern Palace farewell; Emperor Wu thought he did not give full sincerity and harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: After he left Gaozu sent Xun Boyu with border orders; he set out by night and could not bid the Eastern Palace farewell; Emperor Wu thought him insincere and resented it.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，詔稱其與荀伯玉構扇邊荒，誅之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming an edict said he with Xun Boyu had stirred the border wilds and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year one an edict accused him and Xun Boyu of stirring the border wilds and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 故人無敢至者，獨有前豫州主簿夏侯恭叔出家財為殯，時人以比欒布。

translations.literal: No old friend dared come; only the former Yuzhou chief clerk Xiahou Gongshu spent his family's wealth for the burial; men of the time compared him to Luan Bu.
translations.idiomatic: No old friend dared come; only former Yuzhou chief clerk Xiahou Gongshu spent family wealth on the burial—men compared him to Luan Bu.

sentences.zh: 恭叔譙國人，崇祖為豫州，聞其才義，辟為主簿，兼掌書翰。

translations.literal: Gongshu was a man of Qiao; when Chongzu was Inspector of Yuzhou he heard his talent and righteousness and recruited him as chief clerk, also managing documents.
translations.idiomatic: Gongshu of Qiao: when Chongzu governed Yuzhou he heard his talent and recruited him as chief clerk and scribe.

sentences.zh: 高帝即位，方鎮皆有賀表，王儉見崇祖啟，咨嗟良久，曰：「此恭叔辭也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended, each frontier post had congratulatory memorials; Wang Jian saw Chongzu's memorial, sighed long, and said, "This is Gongshu's wording."
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu ascended each frontier sent congratulations; Wang Jian saw Chongzu's memorial, sighed, and said: "This is Gongshu's wording."

sentences.zh: 」時宋氏封爵，隨運遷改，恭叔以柳元景中興元勳，劉勉殞身王事，不宜見廢，上表論之，甚有義理。

translations.literal: At the time Song enfeoffments shifted with the times; Gongshu because Liu Yuanjing was a founding merit of the restoration and Liu Mian died for the royal house should not be abolished—he memorialized arguing this with strong reason.
translations.idiomatic: Song enfeoffments shifted with the times; Gongshu argued Liu Yuanjing's restoration merit and Liu Mian's death for the throne should not be abolished—his memorial had strong reason.

sentences.zh: 事雖不從，優詔見答。

translations.literal: Though the affair was not followed, a gracious edict answered.
translations.idiomatic: Though rejected, a gracious edict answered.

sentences.zh: 後為竟陵令，惠化大行。

translations.literal: Later he was Magistrate of Jingling; benevolent transformation greatly spread.
translations.idiomatic: Later as magistrate of Jingling benevolent rule spread widely.

sentences.zh: 木連理，上有光如燭，咸以善政所致。

translations.literal: Trees joined in one trunk with light on them like candles; all took it as caused by good government.
translations.idiomatic: Trees joined in one trunk with candle-like light; all attributed it to good government.

sentences.zh: 榮祖字華先，崇祖從父兄也。

translations.literal: Rongzu, courtesy name Huaxian, was Chongzu's elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu, styled Huaxian, was Chongzu's elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 父諒之，宋北中郎府參軍。

translations.literal: His father Liangzhi was an aide in the Northern Army of Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liangzhi was an aide in the Northern Army under a Song prince.

sentences.zh: 榮祖少學騎射，或曰：「何不學書？

translations.literal: Rongzu from youth studied riding and archery; someone said, "Why not study books?"
translations.idiomatic: From youth Rongzu studied riding and archery; someone said: "Why not study books?"

sentences.zh: 」榮祖曰：「曹操、曹丕，上馬橫槊，下馬談論，此可不負飲食矣。

translations.literal: Rongzu said, "Cao Cao and Cao Pi—mounted they level spears, dismounted they discuss doctrine; this can already repay one's food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu said: "Cao Cao and Cao Pi—mounted they level spears, dismounted they discuss doctrine; that already repays one's keep.

sentences.zh: 君輩無自全之伎，何異犬羊乎。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen have no skill to preserve yourselves—how are you different from dogs and sheep?"
translations.idiomatic: You have no skill to preserve yourselves—what are you but dogs and sheep?"

sentences.zh: 宋孝建中，為後軍參軍。

translations.literal: In Xiaojian of Song he was aide in the Rear Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song's Xiaojian reign he was aide in the rear army.

sentences.zh: 伯父豫州刺史護之子襲祖為淮陽太守，孝武以事徙之嶺南，護之不食而死。

translations.literal: His uncle Inspector of Yuzhou Huzhi's son Xizu's was Administrator of Huaiyang; Emperor Xiaowu for an affair moved him to the southern mountains; Huzhi starved himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Huzhi's son Xizu governed Huaiyang; Emperor Xiaowu for an affair banished him to the southern mountains; Huzhi starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 帝疾篤，又使殺襲祖。

translations.literal: When the Emperor's illness was severe he again sent to kill Xizu.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor's illness worsened he again sent to kill Xizu.

sentences.zh: 臨死與榮祖書曰：「弟嘗勸我危行言遜，今果敗矣。」

translations.literal: Facing death Xizu wrote Rongzu a letter saying, "Younger brother once urged me to walk on the edge and speak humbly—now indeed I am ruined."
translations.idiomatic: Facing death Xizu wrote Rongzu: "You once urged me to walk the edge and speak humbly—now I am ruined indeed."

sentences.zh: 榮祖善彈，登西樓，見翔鵠雲中，謂左右當生取之。

translations.literal: Rongzu was skilled with the crossbow; ascending the west tower he saw a soaring goose in the clouds and told those at his side they should take it alive.
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu was skilled with the crossbow; from the west tower he saw a goose in the clouds and told his men to take it alive.

sentences.zh: 於是彈其兩翅，毛脫盡，墜地無傷，養毛生後飛去，其妙如此。

translations.literal: Thereupon he shot both wings; the feathers fell clean; it dropped to earth unharmed; when the feathers regrew it flew away again—such was his skill.
translations.idiomatic: He shot both wings; feathers fell clean; it dropped unharmed; when feathers regrew it flew away—such was his skill.

sentences.zh: 元徽末，蒼梧凶狂，恒欲危害高帝。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui Cangwu was vicious and wild and always wished to harm Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanhui's end Cangwu was vicious and always wished to harm Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 帝欲奔廣陵起事，荀伯玉等皆贊成之。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to flee to Guangling to raise troops; Xun Boyu and others all approved.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wished to flee to Guangling to raise troops; Xun Boyu and others approved.

sentences.zh: 榮祖諫曰：「領府去台百步，公走人豈不知。

translations.literal: Rongzu remonstrated, "The chief office is a hundred paces from the throne—if my lord runs, how would men not know?
translations.idiomatic: Rongzu remonstrated: "Headquarters is a hundred paces from the throne—if you run, who will not know?

sentences.zh: 若單騎輕行，廣陵人一旦閉門不相受，公欲何之？

translations.literal: If you go alone lightly, once Guangling men shut the gate and will not receive you, whither would my lord go?
translations.idiomatic: If you ride alone, once Guangling shuts its gate, whither will you go?

sentences.zh: 公今動足下床，恐便有叩台門者，公事去矣。

translations.literal: If my lord now moves a foot off the bed, I fear there will be one knocking at the ministry gate—my lord's affair is gone."
translations.idiomatic: If you step off the bed tonight, I fear men will knock at the ministry gate—your affair is lost."

sentences.zh: 」蒼梧明夕自至領府扣門，欲害帝，帝嘗以書案下安鼻為楯，以鐵為書鎮如意，甚壯大，以備不虞，欲以代杖。

translations.literal: The next evening Cangwu himself came to headquarters and knocked, wishing to harm Gaozu; Gaozu had once placed a nose-shield under the writing desk and an iron book-weight like a ruyi, very stout, prepared against the unforeseen, intending to use it in place of a staff.
translations.idiomatic: The next evening Cangwu came to headquarters to kill Gaozu; Gaozu had placed a nose-shield under the desk and a stout iron book-weight like a ruyi as staff against surprise.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧至府，而曰：「且申今夕，須至一處作適，還當取奴。

translations.literal: Cangwu reached headquarters and said, "For tonight let us delay; I must go somewhere for sport—returning I will take the slave."
translations.idiomatic: Cangwu arrived and said: "Tonight let us delay; I must go elsewhere for sport—returning I will take the slave."

sentences.zh: 」尋遇殺。

translations.literal: Soon he met death.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was killed.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝謂榮祖曰：「不用卿言，幾無所成。

translations.literal: Gaozu told Rongzu, "Had I not used your words, I would nearly have accomplished nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told Rongzu: "Without your words I would nearly have failed entirely."

sentences.zh: 」豫佐命勳，封將樂縣子。

translations.literal: For assisting the founding merit he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiangle.
translations.idiomatic: For assisting the founding he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Jiangle.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，為尋陽相、南新蔡太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was Administrator of Xunyang and Administrator of South Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year two he was administrator of Xunyang and South Xincai.

sentences.zh: 被告作大形棺材盛仗，使鄉人載度江北，案驗無實，見原。

translations.literal: Accused of making a large coffin to hold weapons and having countrymen carry it across the river north—the investigation found no truth—and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of making a great coffin for weapons and having countrymen carry it north—the charge failed—and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後拜兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，巴東王子響事，方鎮皆啟稱子響為逆，榮祖曰：「此非所宜言，政應雲劉寅等孤負恩獎，逼迫巴東，使至於此。

translations.literal: At first in Prince of Badong's affair every frontier post memorialized calling the prince a rebel; Rongzu said, "This is not what should be said—properly one should say Liu Yin and others betrayed grace and pressed Badong until it came to this."
translations.idiomatic: In Prince of Badong's affair every frontier called the prince rebel; Rongzu said: "That is not fit—properly Liu Yin and others betrayed grace and drove Badong to this."

sentences.zh: 」時諸啟皆不得通，事平後，上乃省視，以榮祖為知言。

translations.literal: At the time none of the memorials could pass; after the affair was settled the Emperor reviewed them and judged Rongzu's words knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Then no memorial passed; after the affair the Emperor reviewed them and judged Rongzu knowing.

sentences.zh: 九年卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year nine.

sentences.zh: 從弟曆生，亦為驍將，位太子右率。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Lisheng was also a fierce general and held the post of Right Leader of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Lisheng was also a fierce general and right leader of the heir.

sentences.zh: 性苛暴，與始安王遙光同反，伏誅。

translations.literal: By nature he was harsh and violent; with Prince of Shian Yao Guang he rebelled together and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh and violent by nature, he rebelled with Prince of Shian Yao Guang and was executed.

sentences.zh: 憘伯少負氣豪俠，妙解射雉，尤為武帝所重，以為直合將軍。

translations.literal: Xibo from youth bore a fierce, heroic spirit and was marvelously skilled at shooting pheasants; the Emperor especially valued him and made him General of the Direct Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xibo from youth was fierce and heroic and marvelously skilled at shooting pheasants; the Emperor valued him and made him general of the direct guard.

sentences.zh: 與王文和俱任，頗以地勢陵之。

translations.literal: He served together with Wang Wenhe and somewhat looked down on him by position.
translations.idiomatic: He served with Wang Wenhe and somewhat looked down on him by rank.

sentences.zh: 後出為巴西、梓潼二郡太守，時文和為益州刺史，曰：「每憶昔日俱在合下，卿時視我，如我今日見卿。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Administrator of Baxi and Zitong; at the time Wenhe was Inspector of Yizhou and said, "Each time I recall how we were together under the guard—then you looked at me as I today look at you."
translations.idiomatic: Later as administrator of Baxi and Zitong, when Wenhe was inspector of Yizhou he said: "I recall when we served together—you looked at me as I now look at you."

sentences.zh: 」因誣其罪，馳信啟之，又輒遣蕭寅代憘伯為郡。

translations.literal: Thereupon he framed a charge against him, sent a fast letter to report, and again hastily sent Xiao Yin to replace Xibo in the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He framed a charge, reported by fast letter, and hastily sent Xiao Yin to replace Xibo.

sentences.zh: 憘伯亦別遣啟台，閉門待報，寅以兵圍之。

translations.literal: Xibo also sent a separate memorial to the throne, shut his gates awaiting reply; Yin surrounded him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xibo memorialized separately, shut his gates awaiting reply; Yin surrounded him with troops.

sentences.zh: 齊明帝輔政，知其無罪，不欲乖文和，乃敕憘伯解郡。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Qi assisted government and knew him guiltless yet did not wish to cross Wenhe and ordered Xibo to relinquish the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming assisting government knew him guiltless yet would not cross Wenhe and ordered Xibo to relinquish the commandery.

sentences.zh: 還為寅軍所躡，束手受害。

translations.literal: On return he was trailed by Yin's army, bound hand and victim.
translations.idiomatic: Returning he was trailed by Yin's army and killed bound hand and foot.

sentences.zh: 閎弟子曇深，以行義稱。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother's son Tanshen was famed for righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's nephew Tanshen was famed for righteous conduct.

sentences.zh: 為臨城縣，罷歸，得錢十萬，以買宅奉兄，退無私蓄。

translations.literal: As Magistrate of Lincheng, on dismissal and return he got a hundred thousand cash, bought a residence to serve his elder brother, and retired without private savings.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Lincheng, dismissed and returned with a hundred thousand cash, he bought a house for his elder brother and kept no private savings.

sentences.zh: 先是劉楷為交州，謂王儉曰：「欲一人為南土所聞者同行。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Kai was Inspector of Jiaozhou and said to Wang Jian, "I wish one man known in the southern lands to go together."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Kai as inspector of Jiaozhou told Wang Jian: "I want one man known in the south to go with me."

sentences.zh: 」儉良久曰：「得之矣。

translations.literal: Jian after long silence said, "I have got him."
translations.idiomatic: Jian was silent long, then said: "I have him."

sentences.zh: 昔垣閎為交州，閎弟閱又為九真郡，皆著信南中。

translations.literal: Formerly Yuan Hong was Inspector of Jiaozhou; Hong's younger brother Yue was also Administrator of Jiuzhen—both were trusted in the southern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Yuan Hong governed Jiaozhou; Hong's brother Yue governed Jiuzhen—both trusted in the south.

sentences.zh: 羽林監曇深者，閱之子也。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Tanshen is Yue's son.
translations.idiomatic: Feathered Forest supervisor Tanshen is Yue's son.

sentences.zh: 雅有學行，當令同行。

translations.literal: He has learning and conduct in elegance and should be sent together.
translations.idiomatic: He has learning and conduct and should go along.

sentences.zh: 」及隨楷，未至交州而卒，楷惆悵良久。

translations.literal: Following Kai he died before reaching Jiaozhou; Kai grieved long.
translations.idiomatic: Following Kai he died before reaching Jiaozhou; Kai grieved long.

sentences.zh: 曇深妻鄭氏，字獻英，滎陽人，時年二十，子文凝始生，仍隨楷到鎮。

translations.literal: Tanshen's wife Lady Zheng, styled Xianying, a woman of Xingyang, was then twenty; her son Wennin was just born; she still followed Kai to the post.
translations.idiomatic: Tanshen's wife Lady Zheng, styled Xianying, of Xingyang, was then twenty; son Wennin just born; she still followed Kai to the post.

sentences.zh: 晝夜紡織，傍無親援，年既盛美，甚有容德，自厲冰霜，無敢望其門者。

translations.literal: Day and night she spun and wove; at her side no kin to aid; her years were in full beauty; she had much grace in bearing; she hardened herself like frost and ice—none dared look toward her gate.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night she spun; no kin near; young and beautiful yet hard as frost—none dared approach her gate.

sentences.zh: 居一年，私裝了，乃告楷求還。

translations.literal: After one year her private preparations were complete and she told Kai asking to return.
translations.idiomatic: After a year her preparations were complete and she asked Kai to return.

sentences.zh: 楷大驚曰：「去鄉萬里，固非孀婦所濟」，遂不許。

translations.literal: Kai greatly alarmed said, "Ten thousand li from home—surely not what a widow can manage," and would not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Kai alarmed said: "Ten thousand li from home—surely not for a widow," and refused.

sentences.zh: 鄭又曰：「垣氏羇魂不反，而其孤藐幼，妾若一同灰壤，則何面目以見先姑。

translations.literal: Lady Zheng again said, "The Yuan clan's wandering soul does not return, yet their orphaned and tender remain; if I share one ash with them, with what face could I see my husband's mother before?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zheng said: "Yuan's wandering soul does not return; their orphans remain; if I become ash with them, with what face see my mother-in-law?"

sentences.zh: 」因大悲泣。

translations.literal: Thereupon she wailed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: She wailed greatly.

sentences.zh: 楷愴然許之，厚為之送，於是間關危險，遂得至鄉。

translations.literal: Kai mournfully permitted; he sent her off richly; thus through peril and hardship she reached home.
translations.idiomatic: Kai mournfully agreed and sent her off richly; through peril she reached home.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，乃曰：「可以下見先姑矣。

translations.literal: When burial was finished she said, "Now I can go down to see my husband's mother."
translations.idiomatic: When burial was done she said: "Now I can go down to see my mother-in-law."

sentences.zh: 」時文凝年甫四歲，親教經禮，訓以義方，州裏稱美。

translations.literal: At the time Wennin was just four; she personally taught rites and classics, instructing in righteous method; the district praised her.
translations.idiomatic: Wennin was four; she taught rites and classics; the district praised her.

sentences.zh: 又有吳興丘景賓，字彥先，亦以節義聞。

translations.literal: There was also Qiu Jingbin of Wuxing, styled Yanxian, also famed for integrity and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Also Qiu Jingbin of Wuxing, styled Yanxian, was famed for integrity.

sentences.zh: 父康祖，無錫令，亡後，僮僕數十人及宅宇產畜，景賓悉讓與兄鎮之。

translations.literal: His father Kangzu was Magistrate of Wuxi; after death the male and female servants numbered several tens and the residence, fields, and livestock—Jingbin all yielded to his elder brother Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kangzu was magistrate of Wuxi; after death servants, house, fields, and livestock—Jingbin yielded all to elder brother Zhenzhi.

sentences.zh: 鎮之又推齋屋三間與之，亦不肯受。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi again pushed three rooms of the study house to him; he also would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi offered three study rooms; he would not accept.

sentences.zh: 太守孔山士歎曰：「聞柳下惠之風，貪夫廉，懦夫有立志。

translations.literal: Administrator Kong Shanshi sighed, "Hearing the wind of Liuxiahui, the greedy grow honest and the coward finds resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Administrator Kong Shanshi sighed: "Hearing Liuxiahui's wind, the greedy grow honest and cowards find resolve.

sentences.zh: 復見之矣。

translations.literal: I see it again."
translations.idiomatic: I see it again."

sentences.zh: 」終於奉朝請。

translations.literal: He ended as Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as court gentleman for attendance.

sentences.zh: 張興世字文德，竟陵人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Xingshi, courtesy name Wende, was a man of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingshi, styled Wende, came from Jingling.

sentences.zh: 本單名世，宋明帝益為興世。

translations.literal: Originally his single name was Shi; Emperor Ming of Song added Xing to make Xingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Originally named Shi; Emperor Ming added Xing to make Xingshi.

sentences.zh: 少家貧，白衣隨王玄謨代蠻。

translations.literal: From youth his family was poor; in white clothes he followed Wang Xuemo against the Man.
translations.idiomatic: Poor from youth, in plain clothes he followed Wang Xuemo against the Man.

sentences.zh: 後隨孝武鎮尋陽，補南中郎參軍督護，從入討元凶。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Xiaowu garrisoning Xunyang, was appointed Aide in the Southern Army with command protection, and followed the entry to punish the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Xiaowu at Xunyang, became aide in the southern army with command protection, and joined the march to punish the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 及南郡王義宣反，又隨玄謨出梁山，有戰功。

translations.literal: When Prince of Nan Commandery Liu Yixuan rebelled he again followed Xuemo out to Liangshan and had merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yixuan rebelled he again followed Xuemo to Liangshan and won merit.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，四方反叛，進興世龍驤將軍，領水軍拒南賊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended, the four directions rebelled; Xingshi was promoted to Flying Dragon General and led the river force to resist the southern rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended, rebels rose everywhere; Xingshi was made Flying Dragon General and led the fleet against southern rebels.

sentences.zh: 時台軍據赭圻，朝廷遣吏部尚書褚彥回就赭圻行選。

translations.literal: At the time the court army held Zheqi; the court sent Master of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yanhui to Zheqi to conduct selection.
translations.idiomatic: The court army held Zheqi; the court sent Master of Personnel Chu Yanhui to Zheqi to conduct selection.

sentences.zh: 是役也，皆先戰授位，檄板不供，由是有黃紙劄。

translations.literal: In this campaign all first received rank after battle; proclamation boards were insufficient, hence there were yellow-paper chits.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign ranks came after battle; boards ran short, so yellow-paper chits were used.

sentences.zh: 南賊屯在鵲尾，既相持久不決，興世建議曰：「賊據上流，兵張地勝，今以奇兵潛出其上，使其首尾周惶，進退疑沮，糧運艱礙，乃制勝之奇。

translations.literal: The southern rebels encamped at Quewei; as they faced each other long without decision, Xingshi proposed, "The rebels hold the upper stream—their soldiers spread over advantageous ground; now with strange troops secretly go out above them and make head and tail anxious on every side, advance and retreat doubting and discouraged, grain transport difficult—this is the strange stroke of victory."
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held Quewei; stalemate lingered. Xingshi proposed: "They hold the upper stream on advantageous ground; send odd troops secretly above to make head and tail anxious, advance and retreat doubtful, grain hard to move—that is the winning stroke."

sentences.zh: 」沈攸之、吳喜並贊其計，分戰士七千配之。

translations.literal: Shen Youzhi and Wu Xi both praised his plan and assigned seven thousand fighters to him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Youzhi and Wu Xi praised the plan and gave him seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 興世乃令輕舸泝流而上，旋復回還，一二日中輒復如此，使賊不為之防。

translations.literal: Xingshi then ordered light boats to row upstream, then turn and return; in one or two days he did this again and again, so the rebels did not guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent light boats upstream then back, repeating for days, so rebels did not guard.

sentences.zh: 賊帥劉胡聞興世欲上，笑之曰：「我尚不敢越彼下取揚州，興世何人欲據我上。

translations.literal: The rebel commander Liu Hu heard Xingshi wished to go upstream and laughed, "I still dare not cross below them to take Yangzhou—what man is Xingshi that he wishes to hold ground above me?"
translations.idiomatic: Rebel commander Liu Hu heard and laughed: "I dare not cross below to take Yangzhou—who is Xingshi to hold ground above me?"

sentences.zh: 」興世謂攸之等曰：「上流唯有錢溪可據。

translations.literal: Xingshi told Youzhi and the others, "On the upper stream only Qianxi can be held."
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi told Youzhi: "On the upper stream only Qianxi can be held."

sentences.zh: 」乃往據之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he went to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: He went and held it.

sentences.zh: 及劉胡來攻，將士欲迎擊之，興世曰：「賊來尚遠而氣驟盛矣。

translations.literal: When Liu Hu came to attack the officers and soldiers wished to meet the attack; Xingshi said, "The rebels come still far yet their spirit flares sudden and strong.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hu attacked the men wished to meet him; Xingshi said: "They come from far yet their spirit flares sudden and strong.

sentences.zh: 夫驟既力盡，盛亦易衰，此曹劌所以破齊也。

translations.literal: Sudden means strength is spent; strong means decline comes easily—this is why Cao Gui broke Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden means strength spent; strong means decline easy—this is how Cao Gui broke Qi.

sentences.zh: 將士不得妄動。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers must not move rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Men must not move rashly."

sentences.zh: 」賊來轉近，興世乃命壽寂之、任農夫率壯士擊走之。

translations.literal: The rebels drew nearer; Xingshi then ordered Shou Jizhi and Ren Nongfu to lead stalwarts to strike and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels drew near; Xingshi ordered Shou Jizhi and Ren Nongfu to lead stalwarts and drive them off.

sentences.zh: 袁顗慍曰：「賊據人肝藏裏，云何得活。

translations.literal: Yuan Yan angrily said, "The rebels hold ground in the liver and entrails of men—how can they live?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yan raged: "Rebels hold ground in men's liver and entrails—how can they live?"

sentences.zh: 」是月朔，赭圻軍士伐木為柵，于青山遇一童子曰：「賊下旬當平，無為自苦。

translations.literal: On the first of that month the Zheqi army cut wood for palisades; at Qingshan they met a boy who said, "Rebels will be pacified below the month—do not torment yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: On the month's first the Zheqi army cut palisades; at Qingshan a boy said: "Rebels fall below month's end—do not torment yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」忽不見。

translations.literal: Suddenly he was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: He vanished.

sentences.zh: 至是果敗。

translations.literal: By then they were indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: By then they were indeed defeated.

sentences.zh: 興世又遏其糧道，賊眾漸饑，劉胡棄軍走，袁顗仍亦奔散，興世遂與吳喜共平江陵。

translations.literal: Xingshi again blocked their grain route; the rebel host grew hungry; Liu Hu abandoned the army and fled; Yuan Yan also broke and scattered; Xingshi then with Wu Xi together pacified Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi blocked their grain route; rebels hungered; Liu Hu fled; Yuan Yan scattered; Xingshi with Wu Xi pacified Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 遷右軍將軍，封作唐縣侯。

translations.literal: He was moved to General of the Right and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zuotang.
translations.idiomatic: He became General of the Right and Marquis of Zuotang.

sentences.zh: 曆雍州刺史，左衛將軍。

translations.literal: He governed Yongzhou and was General of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yongzhou and was General of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 以疾，徙光祿大夫，尋卒。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was moved to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and soon died.

sentences.zh: 興世居臨沔水，自襄陽以下至於江二千里，先無洲嶼，興世初生，當其門前水中，一旦忽生洲，年年漸大。

translations.literal: Xingshi dwelt on the facing bank of the Mian; from Xiangyang down to the river two thousand li, formerly there were no islets or sandbars; when Xingshi was born, before his gate in the water, suddenly an islet arose; year by year it gradually grew.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi lived on the Mian; from Xiangyang down two thousand li there had been no islets; at his birth an islet suddenly rose before his gate and grew year by year.

sentences.zh: 及興世為方伯，而洲上遂十餘頃。

translations.literal: When Xingshi became a frontier lord the islet was already more than ten qing.
translations.idiomatic: When he became a frontier lord the islet exceeded ten qing.

sentences.zh: 父仲子由興世致位給事中，興世欲將往襄陽，愛鄉里不肯去。

translations.literal: His father Zhongzi through Xingshi reached the post of Attendant Within; Xingshi wished to take him to Xiangyang; he loved his home district and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongzi through Xingshi reached Attendant Within; Xingshi wished to take him to Xiangyang; he loved home and would not go.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂興世曰：「我雖田舍老公，樂聞鼓角，汝可送一部，行田時欲吹之。

translations.literal: He once told Xingshi, "Though I am an old farmer of the fields, I delight to hear drums and horns—you can send me one set; when I walk the fields I wish to blow them."
translations.idiomatic: He once told Xingshi: "Though I am an old farmer, I love drums and horns—send me a set to blow when I walk the fields."

sentences.zh: 」興世素恭謹畏法，譬之曰：「此是天子鼓角，非田舍公所吹。

translations.literal: Xingshi by nature was respectful and feared law and compared it, "These are the Son of Heaven's drums and horns—not for a field old man to blow."
translations.idiomatic: Respectful and law-fearing, Xingshi said: "Those are the Son of Heaven's drums—not for a field old man."

sentences.zh: 」興世欲拜墓，仲子謂曰：「汝衛從太多，先人必當驚怖。

translations.literal: When Xingshi wished to visit the tombs Zhongzi told him, "Your guard followers are too many—the ancestors will surely be alarmed and afraid."
translations.idiomatic: When Xingshi wished to visit tombs Zhongzi said: "Your guard is too large—the ancestors will be alarmed."

sentences.zh: 」興世減撤而行。

translations.literal: Xingshi reduced and withdrew in going.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi reduced his escort.

sentences.zh: 子欣泰。

translations.literal: His son Xintai.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xintai.

sentences.zh: 欣泰字義亨，不以武業自居，好隸書，讀子史。

translations.literal: Xintai, courtesy name Yiheng, did not take martial achievement as his own station; he loved clerical script and read histories.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai, styled Yiheng, did not rest on martial merit; he loved clerical script and read histories.

sentences.zh: 年十餘，詣吏部尚書褚彥回，彥回問：「張郎弓馬多少？

translations.literal: At ten-odd years he visited Master of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yanhui; Yanhui asked, "Young Zhang, how much bow and horse?"
translations.idiomatic: At ten-odd he visited Master of Personnel Chu Yanhui; Yanhui asked: "Young Zhang, how are bow and horse?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「性怯畏馬，無力牽弓。

translations.literal: He replied, "By nature I fear horses and have no strength to draw a bow."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "By nature I fear horses and have no strength to draw a bow."

sentences.zh: 」彥回甚異之。

translations.literal: Yanhui was very struck by this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui was deeply struck.

sentences.zh: 曆諸王府佐。

translations.literal: He successively served as staff officer to various princes.
translations.idiomatic: He served on various princes' staffs.

sentences.zh: 欣泰通涉雅俗，交結多是名素，下直輒著鹿皮冠，衲衣錫杖，挾素琴。

translations.literal: Xintai ranged widely through refined and common worlds; his friendships were mostly famous gentry; off duty he wore deerskin cap, patched robe, tin staff, and carried a plain zither.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai ranged through refined and common worlds; his friends were mostly famous gentry; off duty he wore deerskin cap, patched robe, tin staff, and plain zither.

sentences.zh: 有以啟武帝，帝曰：「將家兒，何敢作此舉止。

translations.literal: Someone reported this to Emperor Wu; the Emperor said, "A general's son—how dare he make such bearing."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported to Emperor Wu; the Emperor said: "A general's son—how dare such bearing."

sentences.zh: 」後從駕出新林，敕欣泰廉察，欣泰停仗，于松樹下飲酒賦詩。

translations.literal: Later following the imperial procession out to Xinlin the Emperor ordered Xintai to inspect incorruptibly; Xintai halted his escort, under a pine tree drank wine and composed poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Later escorting the Emperor to Xinlin he ordered Xintai to inspect incorruptibly; Xintai halted his escort, drank wine under a pine, and composed poetry.

sentences.zh: 制局監呂文度以啟武帝，帝大怒，遣出。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau Lu Wendu reported to Emperor Wu; the Emperor was greatly angry and sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Director Lu Wendu reported; the Emperor was furious and sent him out.

sentences.zh: 數日意釋，召謂曰：「卿不樂武職，當處卿清貴。

translations.literal: After several days his mood eased and he summoned him and said, "You do not love martial office— I will place you in pure and honored rank."
translations.idiomatic: Days later his mood eased; he summoned Xintai: "You dislike martial office—I will place you in pure honor."

sentences.zh: 」除正員郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant Lang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regular attendant lang.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮軍中兵參軍、南平內史。

translations.literal: He went out as Aide in the Army of the Pacifying General and Administrator of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as aide in the Pacifying Army and administrator of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，魏圍鍾離，欣泰為軍主，隨崔慧景救援。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu Wei besieged Zhongli; Xintai was army commander and followed Cui Huijing to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year two Wei besieged Zhongli; Xintai commanded troops and followed Cui Huijing to rescue.

sentences.zh: 及魏軍退，而邵陽洲上余兵萬人，求輸馬五百匹假道，慧景欲斷路攻之。

translations.literal: When Wei forces withdrew, on Shaoyang Isle more than ten thousand remnant soldiers remained, asking five hundred horses for passage; Huijing wished to cut the road and attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei withdrew, more than ten thousand remnant soldiers on Shaoyang Isle asked five hundred horses for passage; Huijing wished to cut the road and attack.

sentences.zh: 欣泰說慧景曰：「歸師勿遏，古人畏之，死地兵不可輕也。

translations.literal: Xintai told Huijing, "Do not intercept a returning army—ancients feared this; soldiers in dead ground must not be lightly treated."
translations.idiomatic: Xintai told Huijing: "Do not intercept a returning army—ancients feared this; men in dead ground must not be lightly treated."

sentences.zh: 」慧景乃聽過。

translations.literal: Huijing then let them pass.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing let them pass.

sentences.zh: 時領軍蕭坦之亦援鍾離，還啟明帝曰：「邵陽洲有死賊萬人，慧景、欣泰放而不取」。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Guard Xiao Tanzhi also rescued Zhongli; on return he reported to Emperor Ming, "On Shaoyang Isle were ten thousand dead rebels—Huijing and Xintai released them and did not take them."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Guard Xiao Tanzhi also rescued Zhongli; returning he reported: "Ten thousand dead rebels on Shaoyang Isle—Huijing and Xintai let them go."

sentences.zh: 帝以此皆不加賞。

translations.literal: The Emperor for this gave neither reward.
translations.idiomatic: For this the Emperor gave neither reward.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為永陽太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out as Administrator of Yongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he became administrator of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 永元初，還都。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongyuan he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongyuan's start he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景圍城，欣泰入城守備。

translations.literal: When Cui Huijing besieged the city Xintai entered the city to hold defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Huijing besieged the city Xintai entered to defend.

sentences.zh: 事甯，除廬陵王安東司馬。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was made Eastern Major of Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: When it was settled he became eastern major to Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝起兵，東昏以欣泰為雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised troops, Dong Hun made Xintai Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Wudi raised troops, Dong Hun made Xintai inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 欣泰與弟前始安內史欣時密謀結太子右率胡松、前南譙太守王靈秀、直合將軍鴻選、含德主帥苟勵、直後劉靈運等，並同契會。

translations.literal: Xintai with his younger brother the former Administrator of Shian Xintshi secretly plotted with Right Leader of the Heir Apparent Hu Song, former Administrator of Nanqiao Wang Lingxiu, General of the Direct Guard Hong Xuan, Chief of Hede Fortress Gou Li, and Direct Attendant Liu Lingyun—all alike in covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai with younger brother former administrator of Shian Xintshi secretly plotted with Right Leader Hu Song, former administrator of Nanqiao Wang Lingxiu, Direct Guard General Hong Xuan, Hede chief Gou Li, and Direct Attendant Liu Lingyun—all bound in covenant.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中書舍人馮元嗣監軍救郢，茹法珍、梅蟲兒及太子右率李居士、制局監楊明泰等十餘人相送中興堂。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Palace Attendant Feng Yuansi to supervise the army rescuing Ying; Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, and Right Leader Li Jushi, Bureau Director Yang Mingtai, and more than ten others saw them off at Zhongxing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Palace Attendant Feng Yuansi to supervise rescue at Ying; Ru Fazhen, Mei Chong'er, Right Leader Li Jushi, Bureau Director Yang Mingtai, and more than ten others saw them off at Zhongxing Hall.

sentences.zh: 欣泰等使人懷刀，於坐斫元嗣，碩墜果柈中。

translations.literal: Xintai and the others had men hide knives; at the seat they hacked Yuansi; his head fell into the fruit tray.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai's men hid knives; at the seat they hacked Yuansi; his head fell into the fruit tray.

sentences.zh: 又斫明泰，破其腹。

translations.literal: They again hacked Mingtai and broke open his belly.
translations.idiomatic: They hacked Mingtai and broke open his belly.

sentences.zh: 蟲兒傷數創，手指皆墜。

translations.literal: Chong'er took several wounds; his fingers all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Chong'er took several wounds; his fingers fell off.

sentences.zh: 居士踰牆得出，茹法珍亦散走還台。

translations.literal: Jushi climbed the wall and got out; Ru Fazhen also scattered and ran back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jushi climbed the wall and escaped; Ru Fazhen scattered and ran back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 靈秀仍往石頭迎建安王寶寅，率文武數百，唱警蹕，至杜姥宅。

translations.literal: Lingxiu still went to Stone City to welcome Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin, leading several hundred civil and military men, proclaiming the imperial guard, reaching Old Woman's House.
translations.idiomatic: Lingxiu went to Stone City to welcome Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin, leading hundreds civil and military, proclaiming the imperial guard, reaching Old Woman's House.

sentences.zh: 欣泰初聞事發，馳馬入宮，冀法珍等在外，城內處分，必盡見委，因行廢立。

translations.literal: Xintai at first hearing the affair had started raced his horse into the palace, hoping Fazhen and the others were outside and that disposition within the city would surely be entirely entrusted to him, thereby carrying out deposition and establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the affair start, Xintai raced into the palace, hoping Fazhen was outside and full disposition would fall to him for deposition and establishment.

sentences.zh: 既而法珍得返，處分關門上仗，不配欣泰兵，鴻選在殿內亦不敢發，城外眾尋散。

translations.literal: But Fazhen returned; disposition closed gates and set guards, not pairing Xintai's troops; Hong Xuan in the hall also dared not act; the outside host soon scattered.
translations.idiomatic: But Fazhen returned; gates closed, guards set, no troops paired to Xintai; Hong Xuan in the hall dared not act; outside forces soon scattered.

sentences.zh: 少日事覺，欣泰、胡松等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Within days the affair was exposed; Xintai, Hu Song, and the others were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Within days it was exposed; Xintai, Hu Song, and others were all executed.

sentences.zh: 欣泰少時，有人相其當得三公，而年裁三十。

translations.literal: When Xintai was young someone physiognomized him saying he would reach the Three Dukes yet his years would reach only thirty.
translations.idiomatic: When young someone read his face: he would reach the Three Dukes yet live only to thirty.

sentences.zh: 後屋瓦墜傷額，又問相者，云：「無復公相，年壽更增，亦可得方伯耳。

translations.literal: Later roof tiles fell and wounded his forehead; he again asked the physiognomist who said, "No longer the aspect of a duke; years and lifespan increase—one may still obtain a frontier lord."
translations.idiomatic: Later roof tiles wounded his forehead; he asked again; the reader said: "No longer a duke's aspect; years increase—you may still become a frontier lord."

sentences.zh: 」死時年三十六。

translations.literal: When he died he was thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王仲德受任二世，能以功名始終。

translations.literal: The judgment says: Wang Zhongde received appointment through two reigns and was able to begin and end in merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: The judgment: Wang Zhongde served two reigns and kept merit and fame from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 入關之役，檀、王咸出其下。

translations.literal: In the campaign entering the Pass, Tan and Wang both fell below him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Pass campaign Tan and Wang both ranked below him.

sentences.zh: 元嘉北討，則受督於人，有藺生之志，而無關公之憤，長者哉。

translations.literal: In Yuanjia's northern expedition he then received command under others; he had the will of Lin Xiangru yet not the rage of Lord Guan—a elder indeed.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia's northern expedition he served under others; he had Lin Xiangru's forbearance but not Lord Guan's wrath—an elder indeed.

sentences.zh: 道豫雖地居豐、沛，榮非恩假，時曆四代，人焉不絕，文武之道，不墜斯門，殆為優矣。

translations.literal: Daoyu though his land lay in Feng and Pei, his glory was not grace on loan; through four reigns men did not cease—civil and martial ways not falling from this gate—perhaps this is excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyu though his land lay in Feng and Pei, his glory was earned, not borrowed; through four reigns the line did not fail—civil and martial ways held in one gate—perhaps excellence indeed.

sentences.zh: 垣氏宋、齊之際，世著武節，崇祖陳力疆埸，以韓、白自許，竟而杜郵之酷，可為痛哉。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan between Song and Qi through the ages showed martial discipline; Chongzu exerted strength on the frontier and likened himself to Han and Bai—yet in the end the cruelty of Duyou—how painful.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuans between Song and Qi showed martial discipline through generations; Chongzu exerted strength on the frontier and likened himself to Han and Bai—yet died by Duyou's cruelty—how painful.

sentences.zh: 興世鵲浦之奇，遠有深致，其垂組建旆，豈徒然也。

translations.literal: Xingshi's marvel at Quepu had far-reaching depth; that he received ribbons and raised banners—was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi's marvel at Quepu had far-reaching depth; that he received ribbons and raised banners was no accident.
